The thief, still hugging the Honey-Comb box, runs through a busier shopping area and looks back over his shoulder with a nervous grin. The furry skater pursues him along the sidewalk past stacks of newspapers. As the creature rushes through, the piles of papers fly apart, pages flipping and scattering across the pavement. Nearby dogs on leashes react and lunge; a large black-and-white dog fills the view as it jumps forward, while a smaller white dog stands beside it. Traffic passes in front of storefronts with red and green awnings. Water suddenly erupts in a tall white spray beside the street, and another column of golden cereal-like pieces or debris showers upward near a shop window, adding to the commotion. The thief pauses and turns his head, startled, then keeps running with the yellow box tight against his side. The chase continues past a green awning marked “K MARKET.” A large white animal figure or costume-like shape tumbles through the scene, and pedestrians in suits and casual clothes turn to watch. Ahead, two movers in blue coveralls are pushing a large black upright piano on a wheeled dolly along the sidewalk. The chaos barrels into them: the piano is struck or tipped, its wooden interior and strings exposed. A burst of dust and splinters fills the air. The furry skater shoots through the wreckage, then reappears with black-and-white piano keys comically jammed across his mouth like oversized teeth. He freezes for a beat with wide eyes and raised hands, looking dazed but still eager. The thief keeps moving, clutching the Honey-Comb box. He runs past a construction area where orange-and-white striped barriers and steam mark an open manhole. A construction worker in a yellow hard hat and reflective vest pushes up the round manhole cover from below. The thief passes over the opening, and the furry skater uses the raised cover like a ramp. The little creature is launched upward, flying on his skateboard against a backdrop of tall city buildings and blue sky. He sails between skyscrapers, crouched low over the board, mouth open in excitement. From above, the thief is seen running along the sidewalk while the woman in the pale dress follows behind him. He looks upward, still holding the cereal box and black handbag, as pieces of debris streak down around him. Then the furry skater drops from above and lands on the thief’s back. The thief lurches forward, face strained, while the creature clings to him triumphantly, waving its arms and grinning. The chase ends with the thief bent over under the furry character’s weight, the Honey-Comb box still visible against his red plaid shirt, and the woman close behind. The commercial shifts to a product display on a table outdoors. A large yellow Post Honey-Comb cereal box stands behind a white bowl filled with the cereal’s round, honeycomb-shaped pieces. Around it are breakfast items: a glass of orange juice, a clear pitcher of milk, toast on a plate, and sliced fruit including kiwi and melon. The box front shows the bold blue words “Honey-Comb.” At the end, the scene returns to the building steps. The blond skater boy sits relaxed on the stoop, no longer the furry character, eating Honey-Comb from a blue bowl with a spoon. He wears his red-and-black skater outfit with pads, and his yellow helmet and skateboard rest nearby; the skateboard has a flame design. A Honey-Comb cereal box sits open beside him. The woman stands over him in her pale dress and black cardigan, palms turned up in a questioning gesture, looking at him expectantly. He keeps eating, then glances up with a caught-in-the-act expression.

A dark, stage-like ice surface appears under a narrow blue spotlight. A speed skater in a white racing suit crouches low, one arm tucked close and one leg extended, surrounded by faint white rectangular guide lines that look like design or motion-tracking graphics. The scene shifts into a stylised digital space: the skater is enclosed inside a glowing white sphere with curved latitude and longitude lines, standing on a fine grid floor. In close view, the same skater glides forward through blue light and drifting ice particles. She is a Black woman with long dark hair streaming behind her, wearing dark wraparound glasses and a fitted white suit, her body angled very low and aerodynamic. Back in the blue-lit studio, she pushes off across a textured icy surface. Multiple ghosted copies of her body trail behind her, showing the stages of her stride. White rectangular overlays lock onto her arm, skate, and body position, as if measuring her movement. On-screen text identifies her as “ERIN JACKSON” with smaller text reading “TEAM USA SPEED SKATING.” The visual emphasis is on her precise skating posture: one hand close to the body, the other arm reaching back, skates cutting across the ice. The imagery changes to real competition footage inside an oval speed-skating rink. A skater in a black racing suit, white leg coverings, and an orange-tinted visor leans hard into a left-hand curve. Red cones and a curved red-and-blue line mark the turn on the glossy ice. Farther along the curve, another skater in a red-and-white suit appears on the outside lane. The lead skater’s body is nearly horizontal from the waist up, one arm swinging while the other stays tucked, tracing the curve with controlled speed. A close-up follows of red ski or snowboard equipment against a dark, blue-lit background. White pants gather at the ankle above a bright red boot or binding, and translucent white boxes with small yellow points appear over buckles, straps, and joints, suggesting design measurements. The view concentrates on the connection between athlete, boot, and board, showing fasteners, edges, and mechanical details. The setting opens to a snowy mountain course with sculpted jumps. A skier launches off a white ramp, skis crossed or angled beneath them, rotating in the air against a pale mountain backdrop. The skier’s movement is then transformed into graphic, high-contrast visuals: first a blue-and-green heat-map-like mountain scene with the athlete in orange-red, then a black silhouette of a skier over a stark white snowy background with blue crosshair lines, and then a vivid red, orange, and yellow field where the skier’s blue silhouette is surrounded by looping circular lines and dotted arcs that trace curves through the air. A snowboarder in a red helmet and red-and-white outerwear rides through a snowy course marked by turquoise-blue lines and slalom gates. The athlete sits low on the board with one arm raised for balance, carving through the course in a compact, controlled posture. A studio close-up shows a red boot and binding on a snowboard, with snow-like particles floating in blue light. More white rectangular overlays and yellow design points appear around the foot, ankle, and board. A male athlete in a white outfit is shown suspended above a blue snowboard in the same dark blue studio environment. He has short hair and a focused posture, one arm extended to the side for balance. Text identifies him as “MIKE SCHULTZ,” with smaller text reading “TEAM USA PARA SNOWBOARDING.” The snowboard is bright blue, and his lower leg equipment is prominently visible: a red boot and a mechanical prosthetic component are attached at the board. Close-ups show the prosthetic leg’s red metal structure, hinges, fasteners, and the boot connection, again framed by white measuring boxes. The emphasis is on the engineered joint and how it meets the snowboard. A close, frontal view of Mike’s face follows. He has light skin, short dark hair, a beard, and intense blue eyes, with floating ice particles around him and cool blue light rising from below. He then appears in motion, wearing a red helmet and white outfit while airborne with skis or ski-like equipment, his body twisting in a controlled jump against the dark, snowy studio background. More close-ups return to a red boot on a ski edge or rail-like glowing line. Thin white guide boxes surround the boot, buckles, and contact points, highlighting the exact placement where the equipment meets the surface. A side view of the helmeted athlete shows a red helmet, reflective goggles, and a concentrated expression, with the blue-lit particles continuing behind him. Erin Jackson reappears in the blue studio, now skating directly forward in slow, powerful form. Her white suit stands out against the dark background, and small snow or ice particles drift around her. She holds one arm close to her chest while the other arm and leg extend behind her, maintaining a low racing position. The scene then returns to broadcast-style competition footage: a speed skater in a black suit and orange visor races down the ice toward the viewer. White boards behind the rink display the red “TOYOTA” name and Toyota logo, and a small “LIVE” broadcast graphic with NBC and Olympic rings appears in the upper right. The skater drives forward with deep, rhythmic pushes, blade edges glinting on the ice. A celebratory moment follows. Erin, still in a black racing suit with white sleeves, lifts a large United States flag high over her head. The flag stretches above her, red and white stripes rippling and a blue field of white stars visible. She moves along the rink boards, smiling in profile. Behind her, “Beijing 2022” and Olympic rings are visible on the blue rink barrier, placing the moment at the Olympic venue. The final snowy sequence shifts to a vast mountain face under bright daylight. A lone skier in a red jacket descends a steep, untouched white slope between ridges and shadows. From far above, the skier appears small against the sweeping snowfield, carving a diagonal line down the mountain. White rectangular tracking graphics begin to frame the skier and parts of the body and skis as they approach. The athlete leans into the turn, throwing a long dark shadow across the snow. As the skier cuts harder, a plume of powder rises and briefly fills the view, the red jacket flashing through the spray before the image becomes mostly snow and blue shadow.

A dark, futuristic control room opens the commercial, lit by cool blue-white lines across the floor and walls. Several operators sit at curved workstations facing large glowing screens. At the center, on a circular raised platform, an older white man with short silver hair sits in a high-backed black chair. He wears an all-black outfit: a black turtleneck under a dark suit jacket. The space has a science-fiction command-center feel, with screens showing cereal imagery, data-like graphics, warning symbols, and a pink Kellogg’s Raisin Bran box. On-screen text at the lower left identifies him as “WILL SHAT” and “BRAN AMBASSADOR.” He turns toward the viewer holding a white cereal bowl with a spoon, then brings it forward as if presenting it. The bowl is shown close up in his hand. It is filled with Kellogg’s Raisin Bran: tan bran flakes, dark raisins, and milk. The bowl itself has the red Kellogg’s logo above large blue “Raisin Bran” lettering. Behind him, one of the command screens changes to a bold warning message. Large white text on a purple background reads, “AMERICA: LOW ON FIBER,” over a faint outline map of the United States. Operators remain seated at their consoles, facing the monitors. The man gestures with one hand while holding the cereal bowl in the other, as if explaining the situation. Then a purple glow and misty energy effect surrounds him in the central chair. The glow intensifies, and he disappears, leaving the high-backed chair empty while the warning screens still read “AMERICA: LOW ON FIBER.” He reappears in a warm, crowded bar or pub, materializing in a purple shimmer beside a table. The lighting is amber and cozy, with brick walls, hanging lamps, people seated at tables, and TV screens in the background. He stands between patrons, still dressed in his dark suit, now holding a full-size pink Kellogg’s Raisin Bran box upright so the front label faces outward. The box shows the Kellogg’s logo, large “Raisin Bran” text, a smiling yellow sun mascot, and a bowl of cereal. A woman at the table, an adult with medium-brown skin and short curly dark hair, wearing a pale peach polo shirt, turns sharply toward him with wide eyes and raised eyebrows. A man seated beside her, with light skin and short hair, looks on from behind a plate of bar food. The woman’s startled expression continues as she looks toward where the man appeared. Soon she is holding the Raisin Bran box herself, lifting it beside her face while still looking amazed. The table around her has plates of fried food and drinks. In a wider view of the bar, the group sits at a small round table while a faint purple glow lingers elsewhere in the room, suggesting the man has moved on. The setting shifts to a bright, lived-in apartment living room. Three young adults sit close together on a teal sofa, surrounded by snacks and casual clutter. A coffee table in front of them holds pizza, chips, cans, and other food. Sunlight comes through a window, and shelves, plants, string lights, and glass-paneled doors make the room feel homey. One person wears a yellow knit beanie and round glasses with a soft tan sweater; another holds a blue game controller; a third sits farther left with a bowl. A small long-haired white-and-tan dog rests on the sofa near them. The older man appears in the doorway behind the couch, arms open in a welcoming, “I’m here” pose. The three people turn to look at him, surprised and curious. He steps closer and offers a white Raisin Bran bowl to the person in the yellow beanie. The bowl passes in from the right side near their face. The group watches him, still seated, while the dog lies calmly nearby. He then leans down, looking toward the dog. The dog is shown close up: a small Shih Tzu-like dog with long cream and tan fur, large dark eyes, and a little black nose. It wears a collar with a gold tag that reads “WILL.” The man stands beside the couch, smiling down, while the three young adults sit with the dog between them. A moment later, the man vanishes again in a purple flash near the doorway behind the sofa, leaving the group still seated and looking toward the glow. The commercial moves outside to a daytime tailgate party in a parking lot. Blue and yellow tents, folding chairs, coolers, picnic tables, and people in sports colors fill the area. A Black man with a beard, wearing a yellow football jersey under a light blue hoodie, points upward with surprise. In the wider view, the older man is standing on top of a white SUV parked in the middle of the tailgate. He is still in his black suit, but now multiple small pink Raisin Bran boxes are strapped across his chest and waist like bright cereal-box bandoliers. People around the SUV look up at him. The man on the ground holds food and gestures toward him. On the SUV roof, the suited man clutches the strapped cereal boxes against his body and shifts his weight as if trying to keep balance. Nearby, a large yellow sun mascot appears among the fans. The mascot is round with pointed sun rays all around, a big smiling face, blue eyes, and the Kellogg’s Raisin Bran logo on its body. A bald, bearded fan in a black jersey with the number “99” throws both arms high in celebration beside the mascot. The mascot bounces or moves past, its cheerful face turned toward the crowd. The suited man on the SUV looks down, still covered in cereal boxes, then appears unsteady. In the wider tailgate view, he is suddenly gone from the roof, replaced by a bright purple burst below near the food table. A folded tablecloth or tarp catches a pile of small pink Raisin Bran boxes as the purple energy fades, while the man in the light blue hoodie raises an arm and other fans react around the SUV. The final product display returns to the futuristic command room. In the foreground, a large Kellogg’s Raisin Bran cereal box stands on a sleek dark surface beside a white bowl filled with cereal. The box front is clearly visible: pink background, red Kellogg’s logo, large “Raisin Bran” lettering, the yellow sun mascot, and a bowl of bran flakes and raisins. Above it, bold white text reads “HIGH FIBER,” with the Kellogg’s logo above. In the background, the command-center operators and glowing monitors remain softly visible, while the cereal box and bowl are presented as the main focus.

A young woman with short dark hair sits in a dim, warm room, wearing a loose, bright red top, black leggings, dark sneakers, silver necklaces, bracelets, and small hoop earrings. Her face is softly lit as she looks down in concentration. In front of her on a small round table is a thin laptop displaying the Windows 11 blue swirl wallpaper. She reaches toward the laptop, and the centered Windows-style Start menu appears on the screen as a rounded white panel filled with app icons. When her hand moves again, the menu closes, returning to the blue wallpaper. The setting shifts into a glossy, dreamlike blue corridor made of rounded rectangular shapes, as if the woman has stepped into the computer itself. She appears small at first, still in her red top, moving forward through the glowing space. Floating translucent panels line both sides like suspended app tiles. Recognizable logos and images include Xbox Game Pass, Reddit, Spotify, Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp, Pinterest, and game or entertainment covers. Tiny white text along the bottom reads, “Apps and services sold separately.” She walks calmly between the panels, then passes close to a colorful linked-loop icon, an Xbox Game Pass tile, and a “Halo Infinite” game cover. She smiles and raises one hand as if greeting or touching the floating icons, then begins to run. Her run carries her out into a vast, bright white desert of rolling dunes beneath a deep blue sky. The red fabric of her top flutters behind her as she runs across the sand. She slows and looks upward with a curious, slightly awed expression. Far above the dunes, a sleek purple-blue futuristic aircraft with glowing lights on its wing tips sweeps through the sky. A heavy green off-road vehicle with oversized tires races across the sand, throwing up dust. The woman stands below, small against the wide desert, watching as an armored soldier in green futuristic battle gear appears near the vehicle. The soldier, visually resembling the Halo character Master Chief, holds a large double-barreled weapon up toward the sky. A bright projectile streaks across the blue, and a glowing burst blooms overhead. The explosion transforms into a soft, colorful cloud of purples and pinks, opening like ink in water. Inside that expanding cloud, translucent Windows 11 interface panels appear. A large floating widget board materializes above the dunes, showing “11:11 AM” at the top, a search bar, a weather card reading “55°,” and other cards such as calendar and to-do lists. The woman gazes up at it, her expression calm and absorbed. Her dark shoes sink slightly into the pale sand, emphasizing the surreal physicality of this digital landscape. She drops downward into a grand, old-fashioned library or reading hall. The space is tall and ornate, with multiple levels of balconies, shelves of books, columns, and a patterned black-and-white floor. Overhead is a large mural-like image with dramatic figures and a bright central glow. The woman falls or floats down through the high atrium, her red top billowing around her like a cape, and lands lightly near a white pedestal. On the pedestal sits a closed book and a glowing purple chat-style icon. A tiny green hummingbird darts over the surface and flies away from the pedestal, leading the view toward a huge arched opening in the library wall. Through the arch is a peaceful lake landscape with green trees, misty blue mountains, and still water reflecting the scenery. The woman now stands behind a large translucent panel in front of her, still inside the library space but visually connected to the outdoor lake scene. The panel resembles a Microsoft Teams or chat interface. Close-up text on it includes “Open in Microsoft Teams,” a group labeled “Dance Team,” and messages such as “Kai: Great practice” and “Momoko Fujito: It’s been too long!” with small circular profile photos beside the names. The hummingbird hovers near the panel. Outside, a person sits in a small canoe on the reflective lake beside the tall transparent chat window, making the digital messages feel physically present in the natural landscape. The imagery shifts underwater, with rippling blue light and shadowy movement, then returns to the woman in a dark blue, abstract space with the Windows 11 blue swirl pattern behind her. She holds a dark blue, birdlike or origami-like shape close to her face, studying it gently. The lighting is low and cool, with her face partly in shadow and blue highlights around her. She turns her head, noticing a warm rectangular opening behind her. Through that opening is a real dance studio or rehearsal room with tan paneled walls, polished wooden floor, wall sconces, and a simple wooden chair. A male-presenting adult dancer with a shaved head, athletic build, and black fitted shirt and pants practices inside. The woman watches him from the blue digital space as he moves near the chair. The opening expands into a large screen-like rectangle on the studio wall; the woman in red appears within the blue world inside it, while the dancer stands in the physical studio looking toward her. Behind her, the blue digital space changes into a large painted mural filled with stylized dancers and musicians in bold reds, whites, and blacks. The woman steps forward in front of the mural, her red outfit echoing the red dress painted behind her. The dancer, positioned across the room, faces her with one hand behind his back. They seem to meet through the boundary between the digital image and the studio. She walks toward him with a composed, focused expression. He turns toward her, and they stand close, facing one another in the warmly lit room. The moment suggests connection and collaboration, with the digital portal having brought them together visually. The commercial returns to the laptop on the small table in the dim room. On its screen, the dancer is visible in the studio, and the Windows 11 taskbar is centered along the bottom. A windowed video or communication interface opens beside the dance video, showing a smiling man in an outdoor setting at the top and a row of colorful thumbnails or tiles below. The woman’s hand rests near the keyboard as she looks at the screen, now back in her home environment, using the laptop to continue the connection that the earlier fantasy sequences visualized.

A young adult woman identified by on-screen text as Madison Chock, U.S. Olympian in figure skating, stands on an indoor ice rink under dim, dramatic lighting. She has long dark hair pulled back, red lipstick, and a serious, focused expression. She wears a sleeveless, pale beige skating dress with sparkling beaded details. Behind her, the rink boards are softly out of focus, with a large red “HONDA” sign visible. The scene shifts inside a rally car. Dai Yoshihara, identified by on-screen text as a rally car driver, sits strapped in behind the wheel, wearing a black Honda-branded racing helmet and white racing gloves. Only his eyes and upper face are visible through the helmet opening. He raises both gloved hands to adjust the helmet and visor, then lowers them, staring forward with concentration from inside the car’s roll-cage interior. Another athlete appears in a dark, enclosed sporting environment. Kaysha Love, identified as a U.S. Olympian in bobsled, wears a glossy black helmet with a clear visor and a fitted blue racing suit with red and white accents, including a “USA” patch on the chest. She leans forward over the front of a bobsled, eyes fixed ahead through the visor. A snowboarder identified as Brenna Huckaby, U.S. Paralympian in para snowboarding, stands in a snowy mountain setting. She wears a white winter jacket with a red Honda “H” logo, dark pants, a helmet, and ski goggles. Snow-covered trees fill the background. She begins descending a slope on a snowboard, body low and balanced, orange bindings visible at her feet. Red course gates and white barriers marked “HONDA” line the run. She carves through the snow, kicking up powder as the board edges sharply across the slope. A bobsled races along a curving ice track. The sled is blurred from speed as it hugs the high white wall of the track, with metal railings along the edge. This connects back to Kaysha Love, whose face fills the view again inside her helmet, eyes intense behind the visor. The setting changes to a high-tech lab or design studio. A young adult woman with long hair, glasses, and a white lab coat stands behind a transparent digital display. A red-and-white Honda badge is pinned to her coat. She reaches forward with one hand as if touching a floating control. Blue holographic graphics surround her: a glowing outline of a car, circular interface icons, and panels of technical text. One visible panel reads “PRELUDE HYBRID.” A vehicle chassis sits on a table, and a translucent blue hologram grows over it, forming the shape of a sleek car body. That digital outline then blends into a real blue Honda coupe driving on a two-lane road through open countryside, with mountains in the distance. The car approaches from the front, then is seen from behind as it continues along the winding road, its smooth rear light bar and low, sporty shape visible. Back on the ice rink, Madison Chock now skates with a male partner identified by on-screen text as Evan Bates, U.S. Olympian in figure skating. He wears black, while she wears the flowing beige dress seen earlier. They glide together across the lit ice, holding hands and moving in unison. Under bright rink lights, he supports her through turns and lifts; her hair and dress fringe trail with the motion. Close views of their skates show black and white boots cutting into the ice, sending fine sprays of ice crystals outward. From above, their linked bodies trace graceful circular paths as they spin together. A white, red, and black Honda race car appears on a dusty dirt course, sliding through a wide turn and throwing up a cloud of dust. It transitions to an open-wheel race car on a paved track, red and black accents visible as it speeds around a banked curve. Large white capital letters begin appearing over the action. First, over the figure skaters, the word “THIS” is centered near the top. As the skaters glide hand in hand, the word remains above them. Over a white Honda racing vehicle driving through sunlit dust, the text expands to “THIS IS.” Then over the bobsled rushing along the ice wall, it becomes “THIS IS THE.” Over the blue Honda coupe driving through mountain scenery, it reads “THIS IS THE POWER.” As the snowboarder carves through a snowy forest, the words add “OF.” Finally, over the blue Honda on the road, the full phrase fills the center in stacked white letters: “THIS IS THE POWER OF DREAMS.” The phrase stays centered while the imagery becomes a collage of vertical panels. On the left, the figure skaters celebrate, with an American flag held behind them. In the middle, the blue Honda continues driving on a road. On the right, Brenna Huckaby appears in her white Honda jacket and helmet against the snowy trees. Additional panels slide into view showing athletes in racing suits celebrating and a bobsledder speeding down an icy track, all arranged around the central white text “THIS IS THE POWER OF DREAMS.” The commercial ends on a clean white background with animated Honda vehicles and athletes moving horizontally across the screen. A red SUV, a red sedan, a blue race car, cyclists, skaters, and other small vehicle silhouettes streak across in red and blue bands, forming parallel lines like stylized stripes. In the center, the red “HONDA” wordmark appears in bold capital letters. The moving red and blue lines continue past it, then fade, leaving the Honda name centered on the bright white field.

Inside a bright, plant-filled living room, a shaggy black-and-white dog lounges upright on a cream sofa, surrounded by beige and green cushions. A TV remote rests on the seat in front of it. Through the large window behind the sofa, a bearded adult man in a tan shirt is outside in the garden, handling a lawn-spraying container. The dog’s posture looks idle and cooped up, with its fluffy paws raised and its head turned toward the window. The dog reclines against the cushions with a smartphone propped in front of it. On the phone screen, videos of dogs outdoors appear, including a dog standing in green grass and then an image of a bright yellow fire hydrant. The dog’s furry paw lifts and swipes near the screen, as if scrolling. As the phone remains on the cushion, the dog turns its head toward the window, where the man outside comes into clearer view. He stands on the patio in a sunny, green backyard, holding a white jug with a hose and spray wand. The jug has a bold red label that reads “WEED KILLER.” He looks toward the dog through the glass while holding the container and sprayer, with garden plants and a patio umbrella behind him. Back on the sofa, the dog lies partly on its side with a smartphone pressed near its head, as though using it. Then the dog faces a television across the room. On the TV screen is a bright garden scene featuring Spruce packaging: a green container with a spray wand. Large on-screen text reads, “SAFE FOR USE AROUND PEOPLE, PETS & BEES,” with paw and bee icons above it and a smaller note below indicating “when used as directed.” The TV image changes to a person outdoors holding the Spruce product near a landscaped area, while the same safety message remains large on the right side of the screen. The dog suddenly becomes animated. It sits upright on the sofa, mouth open and tongue visible, then springs forward off the cushions. A set of keys with a paw-shaped keychain lies on a round wooden coffee table. The dog rushes up to the table, stretches its muzzle over the edge, and grabs the keys in its mouth. A close view shows its fluffy white paw and muzzle near a car door and ignition area, with the paw-shaped keychain dangling from the keys. The scene then moves outside to the rear of a small white vintage convertible on a quiet, tree-lined suburban street. Its license plate reads “IH8WDZ,” and the car drives away down the road. In a garden center or home-improvement store, the same shaggy dog sits obediently in front of a tall, bright green Spruce display stocked with bottles and containers. The display is topped with the large white brand name “Spruce.” A woman with long dark hair, wearing a dark top and a light apron tied at the waist, stands beside the display, looking at the products. Shelves of garden supplies and large potted plants fill the surrounding aisle. The dog is then shown riding in the white convertible, presented comically as if it is in the driver’s seat. It wears pale yellow goggles over its eyes, its long fur blowing back, with its front paws resting near the steering wheel. A green Spruce container sits upright beside the wheel on the front seat area, label facing outward. The background is a blur of lush greenery and palm-lined streets, reinforcing the sense of motion and open air. Outside a house in a landscaped front yard, a casually dressed adult man in a white T-shirt, dark shorts, and sandals uses a green Spruce container with an attached spray wand. He points the wand downward toward small weeds growing between paving stones near the edge of the lawn. The shaggy dog stands nearby on the grass, facing away toward the yard, while flowers, shrubs, rocks, and a porch frame the domestic garden setting. A simple side-by-side demonstration appears against dark soil. On the left, a small green plant is labeled “UNTREATED” in white text on a green tag. On the right, another small plant is marked with a green label reading “TREAT,” indicating the treated side. The treated plant appears smaller and more wilted, with little white marks or drops around it on the soil, while the untreated plant looks fresher and more upright. The man kneels beside the dog in the yard, smiling down at it and gently petting its head. The Spruce container stands upright between them, its green label visible, with the spray wand attached along the side. The dog sits calmly, wearing a collar, in front of the home’s garden and trees. A dark gray pickup truck is parked in a driveway or residential street with several dogs leaning out of the open windows. A large green Spruce retail display, stocked with bottles, is positioned upright in the truck bed. The dogs look outward from the cab, including a white dog hanging its front paws over the window edge and another black-and-white dog visible in the back. A large yellow graphic shape sweeps across the scene, transitioning into the final product display. The commercial ends on a clean green-and-yellow graphic background with a large Spruce Weed & Grass Killer container on the right. The product is a green-and-white jug with an attached green spray wand and yellow nozzle. Visible label details include the Spruce brand name, “Weed & Grass Killer,” “Visible Results 1 hr,” and claims about killing weeds and grass to the roots. Icons on the label refer to use around people, pets, and bees when used as directed. Large yellow text on the left reads, “PET FRIENDLY.”

A steep San Francisco street slopes sharply downhill between rows of pale apartment buildings and bay-windowed houses. Cable-car tracks run down the center of the road, and the Golden Gate Bridge is visible in the hazy distance. A red-and-wood cable car sits partway up the hill, framed by the buildings and trees. Inside the open cable car, passengers sit on wooden benches beneath polished vertical poles. A uniformed male-presenting conductor in a black cap and vest stands near the front with a handheld microphone. Among the passengers are a young adult woman with long brown hair, wearing an olive-green jacket over a cream turtleneck and wide blue jeans, and a very muscular Black man with braided hair, a sleeveless bright blue top, pale pants, earrings, and a large necklace. The woman is holding an Oikos drink bottle, while the man has an Oikos yogurt cup. They look concerned as the cable car appears stalled on the hill. An older woman with short reddish hair, large glasses, a pink floral top, a pale jacket, lavender pants, and a leopard-print bag sits beside the man, watching the situation. The young woman hands her Oikos bottle to the muscular man and moves toward the outside of the cable car. He ends up holding both his Oikos cup and her bottle as she climbs down from the side. In black and white, the commercial opens on a high mountain landscape with ridges and distant hills stretching across the horizon. It bounces and leans slightly over uneven ground, yet remains steady as it comes down the slope. Wider views show the car moving along a winding, exposed dirt road high above valleys and hills, with scattered trees and guard posts marking the road edge. Inside the car, the man drives with both focus and control. Sunlight flashes through the windows and across the driver’s face as he steers through the trees. The road surface is rough and dusty, but the car moves quickly and smoothly, sometimes seen from the front emerging through dust clouds, sometimes from behind as it speeds away along a narrow track lined with pines. Meanwhile, the campsite is shown in disarray. The bear has pulled down or collapsed the tent, and camping equipment is scattered around: folding chairs, boxes, fabric, and containers lie tipped over on the ground. The bear noses among the supplies and later pushes at a metal trash can, knocking it over. The campsite is in a wooded area, with tall tree trunks and strong patches of sunlight and shadow. The Rebel arrives near the camp. The man gets out and stands on the raised ground near the car, facing the bear and the wrecked camp. He raises his arms wide, gesturing in a shooing motion. The bear remains low in the foreground near the collapsed tent and scattered gear, while the car sits behind the man, its light body bright against the darker trees. The man steps forward with his arms spread, continuing to wave the animal away. The setting then changes from rugged mountain roads to a paved highway bridge. The light-colored Rambler Rebel with its dark roof drives along a smooth elevated roadway bordered by guardrails. A final line of text is added below, forming the closing message: “American Motors” and, underneath it, “quality built in not added on.”

The camera is laid down near the bow. The words “Less than $30” appear again in dark lettering beside the camera, emphasizing the price as the product rests on the soft white background.

The room is bright and tidy, with bunk beds, shelves, sports gear, posters, and a dartboard on the wall. Three young people are gathered around handheld games: a girl sits cross-legged on the floor in front, holding a small device and concentrating on it, while two blond boys in matching light grey tracksuits with dark stripes and green shirts sit on the lower bunk behind her, leaning forward to watch. A person wearing a pale yellow shirt stands beside the table and reaches down to pick up the device. In the background, the three young players remain near the bunk bed, still watching and playing. On the screen, Snoopy and another small character appear on opposite sides, with a dot representing the ball between them. The display is framed by the game’s white casing, and the word “Nintendo” is visible below the screen. The two blond boys sit side by side on the bed, each holding a Game & Watch. One looks down intently at a light-coloured device; the other holds a darker or reddish device, tapping its buttons with a smile. A dark, spotlighted tabletop scene opens on two young adult players facing each other across a small round table. On the left is a woman with light brown, shoulder-length wavy hair and bangs, wearing a pale lavender sweater. At different moments, new letters come into view, including combinations such as S, U, C, L, and later other mixed letters. The players’ fingers hover over the cubes, ready to point, while the side panels with small peg holes remain visible on either side of the central track. The game continues as a fast back-and-forth contest. The woman and man both lean over the board, scanning the letters closely. The man’s right hand moves near the carriage as if ready to claim a word, while the woman’s left hand stays near the opposite side. More close views show the letter cubes shifting and settling in the brown channel, with hands braced on either side. The players’ posture stays tense and intent, their eyes fixed on the letters. Near the end of the play, the woman appears to win or make a final successful move. She suddenly lifts both hands high above her head in celebration, her mouth open in excitement. The man, still seated on the right, raises one hand partway with a surprised or playful reaction, looking toward her across the board. The Razzle board remains between them on the table, its central carriage now near the right side of the board. The image of the two players celebrating shrinks into a small rectangular inset against a dark background. At the left, an older man in a dark cap, glasses, and a heavy cardigan leans forward with one hand near his face and the other beside a large white dog. The dog sits upright in the foreground, its long ears hanging down and its curly white coat catching the light. In the middle, another older man wearing a black beret, wire-rim glasses, and a pale sweater or smock reclines in his chair, watching. On the right, a grey-haired older man in a dark cardigan and a white apron sits at the board, leaning in as if making a point in the game or conversation. All three men appear focused on the checkerboard and on each other, while the dog calmly faces forward. The grey-haired man on the right becomes the visual focus. His face fills the screen: thinning grey hair, expressive eyebrows, and a lined face. He looks slightly off to the side, then toward the others, speaking with animated facial movements. He turns his head back toward the table, as if addressing the two men and referring to the dog nearby. The view returns to the group around the checkerboard. The man in the cap keeps close to the dog, while the man in the beret watches from the center with his arms relaxed. The grey-haired man in the apron turns from the board toward the others, then looks outward as if answering a question. The two men on the left are shown more closely: the man in the cap looks attentive from under his brim, and the man in the beret sits slightly behind him, calm and observant behind his glasses. The man in the cap then glances downward, as if considering the checker move or the discussion. Back at the table, the grey-haired man leans toward the other two and gestures with an open hand over the checkerboard. The board remains between them, its pieces scattered in mid-game. The man in the beret sits back with his arms crossed, looking at the speaker. The man in the cap rests his chin on his hand, appearing thoughtful. The grey-haired man continues gesturing, then turns outward with a small confident smile, as though explaining something important. The product is then shown clearly on a dark tabletop. A red-orange and blue box with large yellow lettering reads “Gaines-burgers.” In front of it, two hands hold a round, brown, burger-like portion of dog food wrapped in clear plastic over a cream-colored dog bowl. At the bottom of the screen, white text reads: “MEAT BY-PRODUCTS AND MEAT, VEGETABLES, VITAMINS AND MINERALS.” The hands pull apart the clear wrapping, revealing moist, crumbly brown food inside the bowl. The plastic peels away, leaving a bowl filled with small chunks of the food, while the Gaines-burgers box stands upright behind it. The grey-haired man appears again in close view, smiling and looking pleased, then his expression tightens into a more skeptical or concentrated look as he looks downward, continuing the conversation. The dog is then shown eating. Its head bends deep into the cream-colored bowl, long ears falling around the rim as it eats the brown food. A red and blue Gaines-burgers box stands upright just behind and to the right of the bowl, with the large “Gaines-burgers” name visible on the front and a large “12” near the top. The dog remains intent on the bowl, actively eating. The scene returns to the three men at the barrel table. The dog is now in the foreground, head down, eating from the bowl on the floor. The Gaines-burgers box sits beside the bowl. Behind the dog, the men continue their checker game. The man in the cap reaches over the board to move a piece, while the man in the beret watches from the middle and the grey-haired man in the apron leans in from the right. A moment later, the men look at each other around the table, still gathered in the cozy shop setting, while the dog keeps eating. The final product display shows three Gaines-burgers boxes lined up behind a filled dog bowl on a dark tabletop. The boxes are different colors: a yellow version on the left, a red-orange version in the center, and a mostly white version on the right, each with bold “Gaines-burgers” lettering and a large “12” near the top. The bowl of brown, crumbly dog food sits centered in front. Large white text appears across the bottom: “The canned dog food without the can.”

Inside a bright, plant-filled living room, a shaggy black-and-white dog lounges upright on a cream sofa, surrounded by beige and green cushions. A TV remote rests on the seat in front of it. Through the large window behind the sofa, a bearded adult man in a tan shirt is outside in the garden, handling a lawn-spraying container. The dog’s posture looks idle and cooped up, with its fluffy paws raised and its head turned toward the window. The dog reclines against the cushions with a smartphone propped in front of it. On the phone screen, videos of dogs outdoors appear, including a dog standing in green grass and then an image of a bright yellow fire hydrant. The dog’s furry paw lifts and swipes near the screen, as if scrolling. As the phone remains on the cushion, the dog turns its head toward the window, where the man outside comes into clearer view. He stands on the patio in a sunny, green backyard, holding a white jug with a hose and spray wand. The jug has a bold red label that reads “WEED KILLER.” He looks toward the dog through the glass while holding the container and sprayer, with garden plants and a patio umbrella behind him. Back on the sofa, the dog lies partly on its side with a smartphone pressed near its head, as though using it. Then the dog faces a television across the room. On the TV screen is a bright garden scene featuring Spruce packaging: a green container with a spray wand. Large on-screen text reads, “SAFE FOR USE AROUND PEOPLE, PETS & BEES,” with paw and bee icons above it and a smaller note below indicating “when used as directed.” The TV image changes to a person outdoors holding the Spruce product near a landscaped area, while the same safety message remains large on the right side of the screen. The dog suddenly becomes animated. It sits upright on the sofa, mouth open and tongue visible, then springs forward off the cushions. A set of keys with a paw-shaped keychain lies on a round wooden coffee table. The dog rushes up to the table, stretches its muzzle over the edge, and grabs the keys in its mouth. A close view shows its fluffy white paw and muzzle near a car door and ignition area, with the paw-shaped keychain dangling from the keys. The scene then moves outside to the rear of a small white vintage convertible on a quiet, tree-lined suburban street. Its license plate reads “IH8WDZ,” and the car drives away down the road. In a garden center or home-improvement store, the same shaggy dog sits obediently in front of a tall, bright green Spruce display stocked with bottles and containers. The display is topped with the large white brand name “Spruce.” A woman with long dark hair, wearing a dark top and a light apron tied at the waist, stands beside the display, looking at the products. Shelves of garden supplies and large potted plants fill the surrounding aisle. The dog is then shown riding in the white convertible, presented comically as if it is in the driver’s seat. It wears pale yellow goggles over its eyes, its long fur blowing back, with its front paws resting near the steering wheel. A green Spruce container sits upright beside the wheel on the front seat area, label facing outward. The background is a blur of lush greenery and palm-lined streets, reinforcing the sense of motion and open air. Outside a house in a landscaped front yard, a casually dressed adult man in a white T-shirt, dark shorts, and sandals uses a green Spruce container with an attached spray wand. He points the wand downward toward small weeds growing between paving stones near the edge of the lawn. The shaggy dog stands nearby on the grass, facing away toward the yard, while flowers, shrubs, rocks, and a porch frame the domestic garden setting. A simple side-by-side demonstration appears against dark soil. On the left, a small green plant is labeled “UNTREATED” in white text on a green tag. On the right, another small plant is marked with a green label reading “TREAT,” indicating the treated side. The treated plant appears smaller and more wilted, with little white marks or drops around it on the soil, while the untreated plant looks fresher and more upright. The man kneels beside the dog in the yard, smiling down at it and gently petting its head. The Spruce container stands upright between them, its green label visible, with the spray wand attached along the side. The dog sits calmly, wearing a collar, in front of the home’s garden and trees. A dark gray pickup truck is parked in a driveway or residential street with several dogs leaning out of the open windows. A large green Spruce retail display, stocked with bottles, is positioned upright in the truck bed. The dogs look outward from the cab, including a white dog hanging its front paws over the window edge and another black-and-white dog visible in the back. A large yellow graphic shape sweeps across the scene, transitioning into the final product display. The commercial ends on a clean green-and-yellow graphic background with a large Spruce Weed & Grass Killer container on the right. The product is a green-and-white jug with an attached green spray wand and yellow nozzle. Visible label details include the Spruce brand name, “Weed & Grass Killer,” “Visible Results 1 hr,” and claims about killing weeds and grass to the roots. Icons on the label refer to use around people, pets, and bees when used as directed. Large yellow text on the left reads, “PET FRIENDLY.”

A steep San Francisco street slopes sharply downhill between rows of pale apartment buildings and bay-windowed houses. Cable-car tracks run down the center of the road, and the Golden Gate Bridge is visible in the hazy distance. A red-and-wood cable car sits partway up the hill, framed by the buildings and trees. Inside the open cable car, passengers sit on wooden benches beneath polished vertical poles. A uniformed male-presenting conductor in a black cap and vest stands near the front with a handheld microphone. Among the passengers are a young adult woman with long brown hair, wearing an olive-green jacket over a cream turtleneck and wide blue jeans, and a very muscular Black man with braided hair, a sleeveless bright blue top, pale pants, earrings, and a large necklace. The woman is holding an Oikos drink bottle, while the man has an Oikos yogurt cup. They look concerned as the cable car appears stalled on the hill. An older woman with short reddish hair, large glasses, a pink floral top, a pale jacket, lavender pants, and a leopard-print bag sits beside the man, watching the situation. The young woman hands her Oikos bottle to the muscular man and moves toward the outside of the cable car. He ends up holding both his Oikos cup and her bottle as she climbs down from the side. The cable car’s maroon exterior is decorated with ornate gold lettering reading “O’Farrell & Hyde Jones Streets.” The woman braces both hands against the side panel and leans her whole body into it, pushing hard. Small white text appears near the bottom: “DRAMATIZATION. DO NOT ATTEMPT.” Her face tightens with effort as she strains against the cable car, her hair falling forward. Inside, passengers grip the poles and overhead rail as the cable car begins moving. From above, the red-roofed cable car creeps along the tracks up the steep street while pedestrians and seated people on the sidewalk look on. From a low view near a stairway, the car is seen tilted on the incline, with the woman pushing from behind and the passengers riding inside. Back on the bench, the muscular man clutches the woman’s Oikos bottle and looks surprised, shifting in his seat as the car lurches. The older woman beside him turns her head toward him with wide eyes and an impressed, startled expression. In a nearby apartment window, a person in a striped robe and hair curlers looks down at the passing cable car while holding a spoon and cup, watching the strange scene through sheer curtains. The cable car rolls past a storefront sign reading “The Corner Market,” with smaller text advertising coffee and provisions in San Francisco. The cable car gains speed up the hill. On the sidewalk, road workers in reflective vests and hard hats stand beside orange traffic cones and a white vehicle as the cable car rushes past them. The young woman is then seen alone in the middle of the steep street, bent forward and breathing hard, with the tracks stretching behind her. She straightens and thrusts one arm upward, calling toward the cable car, her face urgent. Farther up the hill, the cable car continues away near the crest. At the rear of the cable car, the muscular man stands on the outside step holding the Oikos bottle out, with the San Francisco skyline and the tall, triangular Transamerica Pyramid behind him. He gestures broadly as if returning the bottle. The young woman stands far below near the top of the hill with both arms raised, and a small bottle arcs through the sky above her against the pale blue background and the Golden Gate Bridge. For a moment the road is empty except for the tracks and the bridge beyond. Then the woman pops back into view, hair flying upward from the movement, smiling with relief as she holds up the recovered Oikos bottle. She drinks from the Oikos protein shake bottle while standing on the sunny hillside street. Large bold white text appears to her left: “PROTEIN PACKED.” Fine print along the bottom says that protein and exercise help fuel strong muscles as part of a balanced diet and notes that it is not a low-calorie food. The commercial ends on a black product display. White block text on the left reads, “STRONGER MAKES EVERYTHING BETTER.” On the right are three Oikos products arranged together: an Oikos Pro cup labeled “20g protein” with berries pictured on the label, a large Oikos Triple Zero blended Greek yogurt tub labeled “18g protein” and “Plain,” and an Oikos Protein Shake bottle labeled “30g protein.” The same small nutrition disclaimer remains along the bottom.

At night, a large illuminated NFL stadium sits in the middle of a city, surrounded by streets, parking lots, and high-rise buildings. Bold white capital letters appear across the stadium view: “DANDRUFF CAN STRIKE AT ANY TIME.” The line expands to read, “DANDRUFF CAN STRIKE AT ANY TIME. EVEN IN NFL STADIUMS.” Inside the stadium, under bright field lights, a long-haired person in a fitted blue Head & Shoulders uniform moves through a busy sideline or tunnel area. The uniform has white curved stripes and the Head & Shoulders logo across the chest. Their very long, thick, gray-brown curly hair blows dramatically around their face and shoulders. Other people in stadium clothing and staff gear stand in the background. The long-haired person looks alert and determined, turning as if they have spotted something. They drop low near a wall in a service corridor beside the field, almost crawling or crouching, with their face close to the ground. Bright stadium lights shine behind them, and a blue streak of light crosses the image. Their expression is focused and intense, as if tracking someone. Behind them, an orange, shaggy, puppet-like creature with big white googly eyes is partly visible on the ground or low to the floor. The orange creature is then seen more clearly driving a small black golf cart through an indoor stadium service area. It has a lumpy, mop-like body covered in orange strands, oversized round eyes, and black-gloved hands on the steering wheel. It speeds through a wide concrete hallway with loading doors, carts, bins, and industrial walls. The creature looks startled and frantic as it drives. Back in the stadium area, the long-haired Head & Shoulders figure stands upright with their hair flying high and outward, one hand near their mouth as if calling out or reacting. The blue uniform and white Head & Shoulders logo are prominent. The scene then shifts back into the stadium’s interior service corridors, where the orange creature’s cart is seen in the distance. A second person appears inside a golf cart: a light-skinned, athletic-looking man with short reddish-blond hair and a reddish beard, also wearing a blue Head & Shoulders uniform. He touches the top of his hair with one hand. On-screen text identifies him as “AIDAN HUTCHINSON” and, below that, “DEFENSIVE END.” He looks forward with a focused expression. The orange creature drives toward the viewer down a long, brightly lit hallway, with another golf cart following behind. The pursuing cart carries the two Head & Shoulders uniformed figures. As the orange creature passes close by, its shaggy body fills the side of the view. The two pursuers continue down the corridor in their cart, the long-haired person on the passenger side and Aidan Hutchinson driving. A worker in an orange cap and light shirt pushes a large white barrel across the hallway near stacks of similar white barrels. The barrels have red lettering beginning with “CHIL,” suggesting chili containers. The chase cart approaches from the background. The worker reacts while moving the barrel, and the scene becomes chaotic as the cart nears the obstacle. Low to the ground, the golf cart’s wheels rush past. Inside the cart, Aidan grips the steering wheel and grimaces, while the long-haired passenger ducks and holds the roof support, bracing against the impact or sudden movement. The cart is then seen from behind in a wider loading area, with brown, chunky material spilled across the floor in a trail from a tipped-over white barrel. The worker stands nearby holding a hose or handle, and cardboard boxes are stacked along the walls. The cart continues away through the mess. The chase ends in a tiled shower or locker-room wash area with white walls, blue accent tiles, and a black-and-white checker stripe running around the room. The orange shaggy microbe-like creature is in the foreground, hunched and facing away at first, as if cornered. Opposite it stand Aidan Hutchinson and the long-haired Head & Shoulders figure in matching blue uniforms. Aidan holds up a white Head & Shoulders shampoo bottle with a blue cap in his left hand, while the long-haired person points forward, confronting the creature. Both look serious and confident. The product is shown closer: a white Head & Shoulders bottle with a blue cap, held in a blue-sleeved hand against the tiled shower-room background. The label shows the Head & Shoulders logo and “Classic Clean.” The orange creature looks upward with its big googly eyes, appearing worried or trapped beneath the black-and-white tile border. Finally, in a locker-room area lined with open wooden cubbies, the two blue-uniformed Head & Shoulders figures walk forward together from a doorway. Behind them, an orange burst or splash fills the opening, visually suggesting the creature has been defeated or flushed away. The commercial ends on a clean product display: large bold white text on the left reads “TACKLE DANDRUFF EVERY WASH,” while a Head & Shoulders Classic Clean bottle stands on the right beside a blue bath pouf against the same tiled bathroom-style background.

A dark blue gradient fills the screen as a bright yellow curved line grows into a circle. A glowing yellow point appears on the shoulder area of the woman in the black sleeveless top, visually echoing the earlier pain-target graphic. The two women hold each other briefly, looking calm and steady after the intense exchange. The commercial ends with three Advil products arranged on a wooden bench or table in the foreground. From left to right are a blue box of “Advil Liqui-Gels,” a central Advil package labeled “Ibuprofen Tablets, 200 mg,” and a larger blue-and-red “Advil Dual Action” package labeled “Acetaminophen + Ibuprofen,” with a red banner stating “CONTAINS 2 MEDICINES.” The gym remains softly blurred in the background, with the fighters moving behind the products. The Haleon logo appears in the upper right. Small text at the bottom reads “Use as directed.” Large white words appear above the products: “THAT’S REAL,” completing the closing message alongside the visible Advil product lineup.

A woman with very short hair, hoop earrings, and a gray button-up shirt stands beside tall white curtains in a bright room. CALCULATE.” Smaller text underneath says, “Know exactly how much you need at every step of your project,” though parts of it blur as the phone moves. On the screen is a Home Depot video page with a large play button and visible text: “HOW TO INSTALL Hardwood Flooring.” A finger taps the play button. He presses a plank flat with his hands, smiles down at his work, and then uses a small yellow-and-black rubber mallet to tap a piece into place, aligning the flooring. A phone screen then shows a Home Depot delivery option. A tile with a small truck icon reads “Scheduled Delivery,” and a finger presses it; the tile turns orange to indicate it has been selected. Outside a house, a Home Depot delivery worker wearing a dark cap, dark shirt, khaki pants, and a white face mask carries a cardboard box. The box has The Home Depot logo and the printed slogan, “How doers get more done.” Other Home Depot boxes are stacked inside the open back of a delivery truck, whose side also bears the orange logo. The commercial ends on a clean white screen with a small orange Home Depot logo centered.

On a sunny beach, a casual volleyball game is underway on pale sand beside a bright blue ocean. A net stretches across the middle of the scene, with waves breaking in the background. Beach umbrellas in turquoise and purple, folding chairs, a lifeguard-style structure, and scattered beachgoers frame the play area. Several adults in swimsuits and beachwear stand around the court. A shirtless man in black shorts with yellow flame-like trim jumps near the net with one arm raised as a ball arcs above the players. The action moves into close views of legs and feet in the sand: the shirtless player in the black-and-yellow shorts lands and jumps again near a woman wearing a long purple floral beach skirt. Sand kicks up around bare feet as people move quickly. Small white legal text appears along the bottom, including a Subway trademark notice. Against a clear blue sky, a white volleyball with colored panels floats high over the net. A light-skinned man in a sleeveless gray top reaches up toward it, then the view returns to the net where several players raise their hands. One person, seen from behind, wears a black shirt over pale long sleeves and a patterned head covering; beside them, a shirtless man stretches both arms upward as if trying to block or set the ball. Large white on-screen text identifies her as “Jackie Biesanz” and says “Lost 95 lbs.” A brown football spins against a pale blue sky, then a shirtless light-skinned man in black shorts with the yellow flame trim crouches with his hands open to catch it. He looks focused, with the ocean blurred behind him. White on-screen text identifies him as “Jason Cromley” and says “Lost 90 lbs.” He catches the ball, tucks it against his body, dives sideways, and lands on the sand, one leg lifted as he slides. Back at the volleyball net, a Black woman with long straight hair, wearing a coral-pink tank top and dark bottoms, looks upward with an eager smile. Other players stand behind her on the sand, including a shirtless man in blue shorts. She moves toward the net, raises one arm, and prepares to strike. White text identifies her as “Myra Jackson” and says “Lost 30 lbs.” She swings over the top of the net and hits the white-and-colored volleyball, smiling as the ball comes close to the foreground. The scene shifts to a large mound of sand on the beach, shaped like a small hill. At first only the mound is visible, with the ocean horizon behind it. Fine white text along the bottom reads that results are not typical and that weight was lost by exercising and eating a reduced-calorie diet including Subway’s low-fat sandwiches. Slowly, the top of a man’s dark hair and forehead appear from behind the mound, then his face comes into view. He is a light-skinned adult man with short dark hair, glasses, and a broad smile. Only his head and neck are visible because his body is buried under the sand. The three beach athletes approach the buried man. Jackie in blue, Jason shirtless, and Myra in pink gather around the sand mound, smiling and helping uncover him. The man’s head is seen in profile as they move around him. White on-screen text identifies him as “Jared Fogle” and says “Lost 245 lbs.” They pull him upright from the sand. He emerges dressed in a purple-to-blue short-sleeved button-up shirt and matching purple shorts. He stands tall among them, still wearing glasses, smiling modestly as they brush sand from his clothes and steady him. He then faces forward with the ocean behind him while the others stand around him; he gestures outward with one hand as if addressing the viewer, while the “Jared Fogle Lost 245 lbs” text remains on screen. The commercial then presents close views of Subway sandwiches arranged on a tabletop. Several open-faced sub sandwiches sit on soft rolls, filled with pale deli meats, shredded lettuce, tomato slices, green pepper strips, onions, and black olives. A bright graphic appears in the upper left: the Subway logo with the words “7 subs with 6 grams of fat or less,” using a large red “7” and a large orange “6” inside a yellow shape. Small fine print along the bottom specifies that the regular six-inch subs are without cheese or condiments such as mayonnaise. The sandwiches fill the screen in layered rows, emphasizing the bread, vegetables, and folded slices of meat. A tighter close-up shows one sub in detail: glossy red tomato slices, green pepper strips, lettuce, onion rings, black olives, and folded pale slices of turkey or similar deli meat inside a roll. Fine print along the bottom reads, “Ask your doctor before starting any weight-loss plan.” Inside a Subway restaurant, the beach group stands near the entrance with repeated Subway logos visible on the bright windows behind them. The space is busy, with seated customers in the background. Myra stands at the front holding the white-and-colored volleyball; Jason stands behind her holding the brown football; Jared, in his purple-blue shirt, stands smiling near the center; Jackie stands to the right in her blue athletic top with a jacket or shirt tied around her waist. They look toward someone off to the right, smiling as if greeting or encouraging them. Finally, Jared sits indoors at a table and eats a Subway sandwich. He wears his glasses and purple-blue shirt, holding the sandwich with both hands. He takes a bite, chews, and looks satisfied. Over the lower right appears the Subway logo with the slogan “eat fresh.” in white lowercase letters beneath it; at the lower left, the website “www.subway.com” is visible. The background remains softly busy with another customer seated behind him, while Jared continues chewing with the sandwich still in his hands.

The commercial opens on a sunlit city intersection with a wide, freshly painted white crosswalk stretching toward the viewer. Storefronts, parked cars, and pedestrians line the street. A young adult Black man with a muscular build walks straight down the crosswalk toward the viewer. She looks outward from above, calm and observant, with the metal stairs and railings forming a grid around her. Back on the sidewalk, the young man walks beside closed metal storefront shutters, holding a red Dr Pepper can in one hand. The white Dr Pepper logo is visible on the can as he drinks, then lowers it and looks forward with a composed, satisfied expression through the diamond pattern of the fence. A girl reaches up toward the window, and the truck side shows colorful menu pictures, a large ice cream cone graphic, and partial “ICE CREAM” lettering. The main young man turns back and gestures toward the truck, pointing as if calling attention to it, while still holding his Dr Pepper can. He passes beneath fire escapes, smiling and looking comfortable in the street setting. An older white man wearing a black hat and light shirt sits outside a shuttered storefront in a folding chair, holding an open newspaper. He turns with a friendly smile toward the passing activity. On another corner, an elderly white woman with short white hair stands with a cane near a small shop. She wears glasses, a light patterned top, a dark skirt, a black cardigan draped over her shoulders, and white shoes. Red Dr Pepper crates or a display stand are visible near the shop entrance behind her. The young man bends down warmly toward her, and they touch cheeks in a friendly greeting. The men react animatedly, raising hands and gesturing, as if cheering or commenting on the play. The young man walks on through a crowded sidewalk, smiling as people pass blurred in the foreground. He bends down to greet a small Black child wearing a white sleeveless top and loose gray-green pants. The child’s legs spread around his neck as he rises, creating a playful, affectionate moment in the middle of the busy street. A taxi driver wearing a dark turban and a beard smiles from the open window of a yellow cab, his arm resting on the door. Pedestrians briefly pass between him and the viewer, then he is visible again, still smiling toward the street. The final image centers on a Black woman carrying a young Black girl on her shoulders in a crowded, softly blurred city background. The woman wears a dark head covering and a sleeveless gray-green top, and she drinks from a red Dr Pepper can. The child, sitting high above her, has her hair gathered into a high puff and smiles while holding onto the woman’s head. To the upper right, a glossy blue-green globe graphic appears and changes into a circular Dr Pepper logo. The red Dr Pepper script sits in the middle, surrounded by the visible slogan text “MAKES THE WORLD TASTE BETTER.” Near the lower right, small white text reads “drpepper.com.”

A warm, staged talk-show set is visible, with a seated studio audience on the left applauding and a television camera crew on the right. The set has tan wall panels, a brick column, potted greenery, two dark upholstered armchairs, and a small wooden coffee table with blue mugs. They are human-sized, scruffy, feather-covered mascots with long yellow legs, oversized yellow beaks, and floppy wings. One is taller and broader; the other is shorter and thinner. The two chicken characters are then seated in the dark armchairs, their long yellow legs stretched awkwardly toward the floor and their wings resting over the chair arms. The small wooden table with blue mugs sits between them and the host. The host stands in front of them, holding the microphone, while the birds look up at him. The host appears to challenge them, then turns away with a knowing smile and makes a sweeping gesture, as if introducing evidence. A large wall monitor behind the seating area now displays a home-video-style scene. In that inset scene, a toddler with dark hair sits in a wooden high chair at a dining table in a dim dining room. Beside the child is one of the scruffy white chicken characters. A large disposable cup with a straw rests near the child, and the chicken character holds a blue aerosol-style can. The child has white foam or cream around the mouth while looking toward the bird. The chicken leans close, the blue can and the large cup crowding the high-chair tray, creating the impression of the bird feeding or spraying something messy to the toddler. Back on the talk-show set, the two chicken characters sit stiffly in their chairs beneath the “Ryan Moore” sign, looking exposed. The woman in pink suddenly reacts. She twists in her chair, plants her hands on the armrests, and pushes herself up with a shocked, angry expression. In the wide view, the monitor behind her still shows the toddler with foam around the mouth. The host stands to the right watching, his arms partly folded. The woman rushes across the stage toward the seated birds. She bends over the smaller chicken character and grabs at it, pushing into the bird’s feathery body while the larger one slumps nearby. A crew member and camera are visible at the far right as the confrontation spills across the talk-show set. The scene then changes to a close-up of cooked food: glossy strips of chicken mixed with sliced onions and red, orange, and green bell peppers. Steam rises from the hot food, and the chicken and vegetables glisten as they sit piled together, suggesting a freshly cooked fajita-style meal. Over the food, the Foster Farms logo fades in: a yellow rectangular label with a red square containing a white chicken silhouette, next to the words “Foster Farms.” Beneath it, white text reads, “Always natural. Always fresh.”

On a busy city sidewalk outside a modern glass-fronted building, a young woman with shoulder-length brown hair stands at an outdoor flower stall. She wears a pale yellow-green dress under a black cardigan and smiles as she looks over bright bunches of pink and red flowers. On the display table beside her are a black handbag and a yellow Post Honey-Comb cereal box partly tucked into a white shopping bag. A young man in a black knit cap, red plaid shirt, dark gloves, and loose dark pants rushes in from behind her. He grabs the black handbag and the Honey-Comb box and bolts down the sidewalk. The woman’s expression changes to alarm; she turns, leans forward, and points after him. The thief sprints past benches outside the building, clutching the bright yellow cereal box against his chest. Several kids sit nearby. One blond boy, about early teen age, wears a red-and-black padded vest, elbow pads, wrist guards, and skater clothes, with a skateboard beside him. He looks up sharply, eyes widening in surprise. His face fills the view as he reacts with exaggerated amazement, then an animated green thought bubble appears above him, filled with giant golden Honey-Comb cereal pieces glistening with honey. He pulls on a yellow helmet decorated with dark spots and flame-like markings, as if inspired into action. The boy is suddenly represented as a small, wild-looking, furry cartoon character: yellow-orange shaggy fur, huge round eyes, a long pink nose and cheeks, black gloves, protective pads, and the same yellow helmet. He rides a skateboard down the sidewalk near parked bicycles and a flight of building steps. Arms out for balance, he gains speed, pops off the board, and leaps high, grinning broadly before landing back down in a chaotic slide. The thief, still hugging the Honey-Comb box, runs through a busier shopping area and looks back over his shoulder with a nervous grin. The furry skater pursues him along the sidewalk past stacks of newspapers. As the creature rushes through, the piles of papers fly apart, pages flipping and scattering across the pavement. Nearby dogs on leashes react and lunge; a large black-and-white dog fills the view as it jumps forward, while a smaller white dog stands beside it. Traffic passes in front of storefronts with red and green awnings. Water suddenly erupts in a tall white spray beside the street, and another column of golden cereal-like pieces or debris showers upward near a shop window, adding to the commotion. The thief pauses and turns his head, startled, then keeps running with the yellow box tight against his side. The chase continues past a green awning marked “K MARKET.” A large white animal figure or costume-like shape tumbles through the scene, and pedestrians in suits and casual clothes turn to watch. Ahead, two movers in blue coveralls are pushing a large black upright piano on a wheeled dolly along the sidewalk. The chaos barrels into them: the piano is struck or tipped, its wooden interior and strings exposed. A burst of dust and splinters fills the air. The furry skater shoots through the wreckage, then reappears with black-and-white piano keys comically jammed across his mouth like oversized teeth. He freezes for a beat with wide eyes and raised hands, looking dazed but still eager. The thief keeps moving, clutching the Honey-Comb box. He runs past a construction area where orange-and-white striped barriers and steam mark an open manhole. A construction worker in a yellow hard hat and reflective vest pushes up the round manhole cover from below. The thief passes over the opening, and the furry skater uses the raised cover like a ramp. The little creature is launched upward, flying on his skateboard against a backdrop of tall city buildings and blue sky. He sails between skyscrapers, crouched low over the board, mouth open in excitement. From above, the thief is seen running along the sidewalk while the woman in the pale dress follows behind him. He looks upward, still holding the cereal box and black handbag, as pieces of debris streak down around him. Then the furry skater drops from above and lands on the thief’s back. The thief lurches forward, face strained, while the creature clings to him triumphantly, waving its arms and grinning. The chase ends with the thief bent over under the furry character’s weight, the Honey-Comb box still visible against his red plaid shirt, and the woman close behind. The commercial shifts to a product display on a table outdoors. A large yellow Post Honey-Comb cereal box stands behind a white bowl filled with the cereal’s round, honeycomb-shaped pieces. Around it are breakfast items: a glass of orange juice, a clear pitcher of milk, toast on a plate, and sliced fruit including kiwi and melon. The box front shows the bold blue words “Honey-Comb.” At the end, the scene returns to the building steps. The blond skater boy sits relaxed on the stoop, no longer the furry character, eating Honey-Comb from a blue bowl with a spoon. He wears his red-and-black skater outfit with pads, and his yellow helmet and skateboard rest nearby; the skateboard has a flame design. A Honey-Comb cereal box sits open beside him. The woman stands over him in her pale dress and black cardigan, palms turned up in a questioning gesture, looking at him expectantly. He keeps eating, then glances up with a caught-in-the-act expression.
