The commercial begins with a flat cream-coloured title card reading “DULUTH TRADING” in large black block letters, with “DULUTHTRADING.COM” in red underneath. It then switches to a bright animated prehistoric landscape. A smoking volcano rises in the background under a blue sky, and a faint “InnoGames” logo sits at the upper right. In the foreground, a hairy bare arm lifts a large pale animal bone like a tool or club. The view widens to reveal a muscular, bearded caveman crouched on dusty ground beside a simple stone shelter made from large slabs, with an animal hide hanging at its entrance. He strikes or scrapes at small stones on the ground with the bone, sending bits of rock and dust outward. A prehistoric woman steps out from the stone shelter. She has very tall reddish-brown hair piled high on her head and wears a leopard-print, one-shouldered outfit with jewellery around her arm and neck. She pauses in front of the shelter, looking unimpressed, then plants her hands on her hips. The caveman turns toward her, looking uncertain and wide-eyed. A black lower-right banner appears with the white text “foe.tv.” He holds up the bone as if presenting an idea or tool. The bone is then shown close to a dark rock face, where it is used like a hammer against a small stone peg. The image transitions through time: the bone becomes a wooden mallet striking a post, and then a metal axe head drives into wood, visually suggesting tools advancing from primitive to more developed materials. The setting changes to a sunny medieval village. A timber-and-stone house stands with a peaked roof, small window, and arched wooden door. A stocky worker in period clothing operates a rope and pulley beside it while the red-haired woman, now dressed in a fitted burgundy-and-white medieval-style gown with puffed sleeves and a black choker, stands in the right foreground watching. She smiles with satisfaction as the building work progresses behind her. The scene moves to a larger medieval construction area with a castle wall and tower in the background, half-timbered houses, scaffolding, and a wooden watchtower. A bearded man in a burgundy cap and vest stands at a worktable covered with small wooden blocks, parchment rolls, and tools. The red-haired woman stands just behind him. He raises a rectangular wooden block, then places it upright among the other blocks as if planning or building a model city. As his hand sets the block down, the background shifts forward in time. Behind the tabletop model, modern glass skyscrapers begin to appear among the older buildings. One tall, sleek tower with a curved, sail-like shape rises prominently in the distance. The tabletop model remains made of simple wooden pieces, but the world behind it is becoming a contemporary city. The viewpoint pulls back above the table and surrounding cobblestone square, revealing the man seated or leaning at the worktable below. The view continues rising until a full city layout is visible: roads, green lawns, clusters of houses, futuristic towers, industrial-looking buildings, and decorative structures arranged like a strategy-game city map. The black “foe.tv” banner remains at the lower right. The game city is then shown on a laptop screen, framed by a black bezel. The laptop displays the same top-down city with modern towers and roads. Other screens appear beside it: a tablet on the right shows a scenic medieval town with mountains in the background, and a smartphone in front displays the “Forge of Empires” logo on a shield and red banner. The devices sit on a tabletop, with the animated medieval village softly blurred behind them. Along the bottom, store badges appear, including “Download on the App Store,” “Get it on Google Play,” and an Amazon app-store badge, while “foe.tv” remains visible at the lower right. The action returns to the animated world, now in a sleek futuristic office high above a city. Curved floor-to-ceiling windows look out over a skyline of pale blue towers, including the same sail-shaped skyscraper. The room is bright, white, and minimalist, with a glossy conference table holding a glowing translucent model of futuristic buildings. On the right, a large, heavyset bearded man in a fitted white futuristic outfit sits in a high-backed chair, facing the table. On the left, the same red-haired woman now wears a slim white futuristic bodysuit and stands near the windows. A stone-age-style boulder or chunk of rock suddenly appears or slides in near the left side of the room, contrasting with the polished futuristic setting. The woman stands with hands on hips, while the seated man looks toward the disturbance, then toward the viewer. The commercial ends on the game logo. Large gold letters spell “FORGE” over a red banner, with “OF EMPIRES” in smaller silver letters below, set over a shield. Small stylised buildings and towers flank the logo, and a bright sky with a village landscape sits behind it.

The commercial opens in a dark, high-contrast setting with a runner’s lower leg and foot visible near a metal starting block. The runner wears a white athletic shoe with bright neon yellow on the toe and sole. Mist or smoke hangs around the floor. The shoe presses into the angled starting block, then pushes off powerfully, lifting away as the block remains behind and a cloud of white vapor billows around it. A tall, pale concrete slab then fills the view, its surface rough and speckled. From the left, a bare human foot extends toward it, attached to a leg in dark clothing. The sole strikes the concrete, and the slab bursts apart at the impact point. White dust, powder, and broken fragments fly outward, making the foot’s kick look forceful enough to smash through the material. The imagery shifts to a car in the same moody, smoky atmosphere. A wheel and the lower rear of a vivid blue Lexus sedan appear close to the ground. Vapor swirls around the tire and the rear bumper, and a round exhaust outlet is visible. The blue car accelerates away on a dark racetrack, its red taillights glowing as it moves along a wide paved curve bordered by low white barriers and lit by bright overhead track lights. Small legal text appears near the bottom of some driving shots, but it is very small and not fully legible. The blue Lexus continues through the night course, seen from different angles as it sweeps along the track. Its glossy blue body catches the light, with sharp body lines, dark windows, and angular red taillights. A silver or light gray Lexus sedan then appears facing forward on the track, its headlights on and the Lexus emblem centered in the grille. The blue car is visible off to the side as the silver car advances, suggesting the two vehicles are driving together or crossing paths on the course. The focus shifts to the silver Lexus sedan in profile, moving quickly along the barrier-lined track. Its low, sleek body, dark wheels, and sculpted side panels are visible under bright track lighting. In another close rear-side view, the silver car’s rear wheel and taillight pass through drifting tire smoke or road haze. The car continues around the course, with the blue Lexus ahead or nearby in the distance, both leaving a sense of speed and controlled motion on the dark track. The commercial ends with three Lexus sedans parked side by side in a dark studio-like space under a cool overhead light. From left to right, there is a blue sedan, a white sedan in the center, and a silver sedan on the right, all facing forward with their grilles and headlights visible. Text beneath them identifies the models and power figures: under the blue car, “IS 200t” and “241HP”; under the center white car, “IS 350 / IS 350 AWD” and “306HP”; and under the silver car, “IS 300 AWD” and “255HP.”

An old, wood-framed television sits in a warm, cluttered attic-like living room with slanted ceilings, shelves, windows, and soft sunlight. On the TV screen, a football game is in progress: a player in a white uniform with a red helmet and the number 88 runs while black-and-silver defenders close in. The ball comes loose as players crowd around him. In the room, a heavyset man in a blue T-shirt over a white long-sleeved shirt, shorts, and a dark cap sits forward in a red leather chair, gripping a football and reacting with his mouth open. Across from him, a man in an orange sweatshirt sits in another chair near a coffee table with snacks and magazines. Between them, a golden retriever lounges in a green leather armchair, head resting on the arm. A third man, wearing a tan jacket and a backward dark cap, moves in the background carrying beer. The golden retriever lifts its head, looks alertly toward the men, opens its mouth as if barking, and sits up in the chair. The man in blue turns toward the dog while still holding the football, and the man in orange leans forward, watching. The man in blue raises his arm, and the room becomes visually chaotic and playful: a football and nearby furniture blur through the foreground as if the living-room action is transforming into the game. A hand in the foreground steadies a pack of white-and-blue Miller Lite cans with gold tops, making the product visible as the scene shifts. The action moves onto a bright green football field in a stadium. Two teams line up, one in white uniforms with orange helmets and the other in black jerseys with silver helmets. Sideline figures, cheerleaders, and yard markers are visible in the background. The golden retriever is now on the field, stretching into a playful bow on the turf, front paws down and rear raised, as if preparing to run a route. Back in the living room, the man in the tan jacket opens or handles a Miller Lite can while the man in orange watches the television. On the TV, the man in blue appears inside the football game, now standing on the field without a helmet among the uniformed players. He crouches near the offensive line as the teams prepare for the snap, while the dog trots behind the formation. The play begins: players surge forward, and the dog runs across the field behind the line. The man in blue, still in his casual shirt and shorts, drops back with the football while large helmeted players block and collide around him. The retriever darts through the action, weaving past running legs and avoiding defenders. The man in blue raises the ball to pass as players in black and silver close in from both sides. The dog sprints downfield, ears flapping and fur shining in the sun. A defender’s legs flash past in the foreground, but the retriever keeps running. The man in blue releases the pass under pressure. Against a vivid blue sky streaked with clouds, the golden retriever leaps high, body stretched out, mouth open around the spinning football. A black-and-silver defender reaches up beneath it, but the dog snatches the ball cleanly in its jaws. The dog lands on the grass and keeps moving with the football in its mouth. A defender reaches toward the dog’s tail, but the retriever slips away and runs low and fast along the field. The football action briefly gives way to a product image: golden beer pours into a tilted glass, filling it with amber liquid and a thick white foamy head. Bubbles stream upward through the beer. Then an amber Miller Lite bottle covered in condensation stands beside a frosty glass mug, with more bottles blurred behind it. The label shows large blue “Lite” lettering, and small white text at the bottom reads “©1995 Miller Brewing Co., Milwaukee WI.” The glass foams over as it is set near the bottle, emphasizing the cold beer. Back on the field, the golden retriever races toward the end zone while defenders chase. A referee raises both arms to signal a score as the dog crosses near the goal line. Stadium walls behind the play display “Lite” signs. A jubilant view follows of the man in blue wedged among helmeted players, grinning broadly, his face and shirt smeared with grass and dirt, with tufts of turf stuck to him. The dog lies on the grass with the football, rolling playfully on its back and pawing at the ball. In the living room, the man in the tan jacket and the man in the orange sweatshirt celebrate, raising their arms and laughing; the man in orange holds a Miller Lite can. The dog then becomes the holder for a kick. On the field, its furry front paws steady a football upright on the turf, and the ball itself has large white “Lite” lettering printed on it. The man in blue runs up to kick while a referee crouches behind the dog. Seen through the yellow goalpost, players crowd the line in the foreground as the man in blue swings his leg and sends the ball upward. A blue banner appears across the bottom of the screen reading “Lite is good.” in white letters, with a round Lite logo at the right. The referee behind the dog raises both arms to signal the kick is good. The final image returns to the living room, where the two seated men continue celebrating in their chairs, lifting their arms and cans while the same “Lite is good.” banner remains across the bottom.

The commercial opens in a stark black-and-white studio space. A casually dressed adult man with medium-length dark hair and facial hair sits facing forward in a large cushioned armchair placed on a round braided rug. He wears a plaid robe or loose shirt, light pants, and sneakers, with his feet stretched out in front of him and his hands resting on the chair arms. The background is otherwise empty and bright. A small black television set appears alone against the same white background. Its screen first shows static, then changes to a Soloflex image: the bold word “SOLOFLEX” above a simple drawing of the exercise machine. A thick hand-drawn black arrow points toward the TV from the left. The toll-free number “1-800-762-FREE” appears in large white lettering on a black rectangular bar across the TV screen, then the TV fades away so the number remains by itself on the white background, with another black arrow pointing down toward it. The scene changes to a close-up of a smiling female-presenting telephone operator in a headset, shown in a vintage switchboard setting. She has styled dark hair, wears jewelry including rings, and holds one hand near her ear while the headset microphone curves toward her mouth. Beside her, rows of switchboard plugs and jacks fill the right side of the image. She looks engaged and pleasant, as if taking the call. On the white background, printed Soloflex materials are displayed: a brochure or manual with a drawing of a muscular torso, and a dark videocassette or video case with a photograph of a muscular chest and the word “SOLOFLEX” at the top. A black arrow points up toward these materials. The toll-free number “1-800-762-FREE” appears again by itself, this time with an arrow pointing in from the right. A delivery worker in a cap and uniform pushes a very large cardboard shipping box on a hand truck. The box is tilted diagonally and nearly as tall as the worker. It is printed with “SOLOFLEX” and shipping markings including “THIS SIDE UP,” “LAY FLAT,” and “DO NOT PLACE ON END.” The worker grips the hand truck handle and smiles toward the viewer as the oversized package dominates the scene. The Soloflex machine itself is then shown assembled on the white studio floor. It has a vertical upright post, a curved support frame, a flat padded bench, a horizontal bar, and a base labeled “SOLOFLEX.” The design is compact and minimal, with dark metal parts standing out against the pale background. The phone number reappears once more, centered on a black bar with an arrow pointing toward it. A shirtless, athletic adult man in light shorts begins demonstrating exercises on the machine. In a close view, he stands beside the vertical post and grips a horizontal bar with both hands at hip level, performing a curl-like movement as the bar rises toward his waist. A drawn arrow points toward the machine’s upright column. His posture is controlled, and his gaze is directed downward toward the bar. The exercise sequence continues with the same man lying on an angled bench, knees bent and feet braced against the machine. With his hands near his head, he curls his upper body upward in a sit-up or abdominal crunch. The machine’s curved frame and upright post are visible to the side, and a black arrow points toward his bent legs and the movement area. He then appears front-facing with a padded bar across the back of his shoulders, squatting on the machine platform. His knees are bent, feet planted, and he rises through the squat with a focused expression. A high-contrast silhouette follows: the man’s body is shown in black profile against a white background, with his legs bent and supported near the machine’s upright post. He curls his torso upward toward his knees, emphasizing an abdominal movement. The vertical post with a line of adjustment holes appears at the left, and a drawn arrow points down toward his torso and knees. The silhouette makes the body position and movement stand out clearly. In a low, close view from beside the bench, the shirtless man lies on his back and grips a bar above his chest for a press. His hands hold the bar wide apart; his arms bend and extend as the bar moves over his chest and toward his face. The machine’s metal frame surrounds him, and a black arrow points toward his chest and the pressing motion. His muscles are highlighted by the black-and-white lighting. Another silhouette exercise is shown in profile. The man holds a handle or bar close to his chin with one fist while a long resistance arm angles back toward the machine on the right. He leans back and lowers his upper body, then pulls against the resistance, the fist staying near his face as the arm and shoulder engage. A black arrow points from the right toward the working position. The phone number “1-800-762-FREE” returns again on the plain white background, with an arrow pointing up toward it. A round wall clock appears, black-rimmed with large numbers and hands clustered around 12, suggesting a short amount of time. A hand-drawn arrow points toward the clock. The visual shifts to a flipping desk calendar. A page marked “MONDAY 13” is visible in bold type, surrounded by blurred duplicate calendar pages as if time is passing quickly. A hand turns the page, and the calendar changes to “WEDNESDAY 15.” The Wednesday page remains centered for several moments, then another hand turn reveals “FRIDAY 17.” The pages are large, with bold black numbers and weekday names on white paper, held on metal rings at the top. The phone number appears again with an arrow pointing down to it. A shaggy, light-colored dog sits alone on the white background, facing forward with an alert, friendly expression. Its mouth is slightly open, and its ears hang down. A black arrow points toward the dog’s head, visually matching the spoken reference to how the dog looks. A close-up of a shirtless torso and loose jeans follows. The waist of the jeans appears too large, with extra space around the abdomen. A hand pulls a belt strap across the front, showing multiple belt holes as it tightens the pants. A black arrow points toward the slimmer waist area and the looseness of the jeans. The phone number returns again, centered on the white background with an arrow pointing upward at it. The athletic man reappears from the chest up, shirtless and sweaty, facing forward. At first the phone number briefly overlays his chest, then disappears. He throws his head back with his mouth wide open, fists clenched near his sides and chest, as if exulting after a workout. His hair is damp and pushed back, his eyes close or squint with effort, and sweat glistens down the center of his chest. He continues pumping his arms and holding the triumphant open-mouthed expression while a black arrow at the left points toward him. The phone number “1-800-762-FREE” appears once more on a black rectangular bar with a downward arrow above it. The final product image returns: the Soloflex machine stands alone on the white background, with the large bold word “SOLOFLEX” above it and the base also labeled “SOLOFLEX.” The commercial ends on the phone number again, now surrounded by many hand-drawn black arrows from every direction, all pointing inward toward “1-800-762-FREE.”

In bright outdoor light on a sports field, teenage boys play a rough flag-football-style game in front of empty metal bleachers and trees. A brown-haired teen in a white jersey with blue stripes and the large number 21 reaches up and catches the football while other boys in purple and white jerseys crowd around him. He runs with the ball, but a boy in a purple jersey, number 85, closes in. The play becomes a blur of motion as the boy in white is taken down, sliding onto the green grass. Only legs, shoes, and the edge of his white uniform are visible as he lands on the turf. The scene shifts to a locker room with gray lockers, hanging lights, and several teenage boys changing clothes in the background. From the viewpoint of an open laundry bin or chute, a shirtless teen with wet, tousled hair stands in front holding a bundled white garment. He grins and tosses clothing forward into the opening. Other boys in athletic shorts move around behind him. The white jersey with blue stripes and the number 21 appears among the clothes being handled, suggesting it is the shirt from the field. Back outside, the same teen in the white number 21 jersey presses the fabric up over his nose and face. In close view, he holds the shirt against his face as if smelling or wiping with it. His dark hair falls over his forehead, and the white fabric covers most of his face. The jersey is no longer crisp; it looks worn and dirty, with smudges and grass-colored stains. Back in the locker room, another shirtless teenage boy with curly hair brings a bulky pile of clothes toward the same open laundry bin. He pushes the bundle forward, and the number 21 jersey lies prominently at the front, its blue number visible amid the white fabric. The boy looks down at the shirt as it rests near the opening, while other teammates move in the background among the lockers. The game continues outdoors. The number 21 player reaches up alongside another boy in a white jersey numbered 61 as both stretch for the football. Arms are extended high, and other players watch from nearby. The ball passes through the group, and the number 21 player turns afterward, smiling. His jersey front is visibly stained and dingy, with patches of dirt around the chest and number. Indoors again, a teenage boy wearing a maroon overshirt over a white T-shirt stands by a red duffel bag. He holds the dirty white number 21 jersey, folds or bunches it, and places it into the bright red bag. In close view, the jersey lands inside the open duffel; hands press it down and zip or close the bag around it. In a laundry area at home, a woman with shoulder-length brown hair, wearing a dark plaid shirt tucked into jeans, pulls the number 21 jersey from the red duffel. A man stands just behind her, watching. The jersey is held up between them; the blue number 21 is large on the front, and the white fabric is heavily marked with yellow-green dirt and grass stains, especially around the chest and underarm areas. The woman examines the fabric closely, pinching and lifting sections, while the man peers over her shoulder with a concerned look. On a shelf beside them sits an orange box of Tide with Bleach, its large white “Tide” logo visible against a sunburst background. The woman lowers the dirty jersey back toward the laundry and reaches up toward the shelf. The Tide with Bleach box is then shown close up: an orange package with a bright yellow sunburst pattern, the large white and blue “Tide” name, and the words “with BLEACH” printed beneath it. A hand brings in a blue plastic scoop filled with white powder. The scoop tilts, and the powder pours out in a steady white stream, suggesting detergent being added for the wash. A demonstration follows on a dark surface. A white shirt with two red sleeve stripes lies flat, showing pale greenish stains on the body. Product boxes sit above the shirts: on the left, a red box labeled “Detergent plus Bleach,” and on the right, the orange Tide with Bleach box. A second white shirt with matching red sleeve stripes is placed on the right side for comparison. The left shirt remains visibly dingy and stained, while the right shirt appears cleaner and whiter under the Tide with Bleach package. Near the end, the woman and the teenage boy stand together in a softly lit room with white window blinds and greenery visible outside. She holds up the now-clean white number 21 jersey, and the boy, now in a brown shirt, takes it from her. The jersey looks bright white, with the blue number and sleeve stripes clear. He looks down at it, then bends his head to press his face into the fabric as if checking or savoring its freshness. The woman smiles at him. The final product image places a box of Tide with Bleach beside a neat stack of folded towels in white and pale pink. Across the bottom, white on-screen text reads, “IF IT’S GOT TO BE CLEAN, IT’S GOT TO BE TIDE.”

The commercial opens in a stylized, computer-graphic space rather than a real store. A large black-and-white “REX” logo floats against a black background dotted with small star-like points. Below it is a purple floor or platform with huge red 3D letters stretching into the distance. The visible words read “EVERYTHING ON SALE,” though at first they are partly cut off by perspective. The logo dominates the center, with a glowing orange horizon line behind it. The Rex logo shifts aside and enlarges as a small, boxy television-like shape appears on the purple floor. The red “ON SALE” lettering becomes clearer beneath it. The small screen-like object grows into a bright blue-framed display window, and products begin appearing one after another inside this glowing square. First, a black audio component is shown close-up, with a label reading “STEREO 2 BAND” on its front. It is presented straight-on, like a catalog product shot, against a pale background. The product image changes to a wide, silver-and-black video or audio deck with buttons along the lower front and dark display panels across the face. It is followed by a black, older-style color television with a deep box cabinet, rounded screen, and two round control knobs on the right side. Next comes a flat black Sony electronic component, low and rectangular, with the Sony name visible at the left and a row of controls on the right. A compact stereo system appears after that, with two speakers standing on either side of a central unit that has cassette or display sections and multiple switches and sliders. Then a handheld video camera or camcorder is shown upright in profile, beige and black, with a handle-like vertical body and a round lens housing near the top. A black rectangular sign with a yellow edge swings into view in front of another electronic component. Large white and yellow text on the sign reads, “REX HAS GONE BEYOND EVERYDAY LOW PRICES!” The word “BEYOND” is especially large and bright yellow, centered among the other white words. The scene then becomes a rapid graphic collage of bold words on a black background. Oversized white and yellow text tilts and overlaps, filling the screen with phrases such as “BEYOND,” “EVERYDAY,” “LOW PRICES,” and “REX HAS GONE.” The letters appear huge, layered, and angled, creating a dense, energetic sale graphic. Near the end, the commercial returns to the starry black background and purple floor with the large red “EVERYTHING ON SALE” and “SALE!” lettering spread across it. The big black-and-white Rex logo floats above the words. On the right, a glowing blue, transparent-looking electronic product shape slides or swings behind the logo, adding to the animated product-display feel. The logo remains the main focus, tilted slightly as the red “SALE!” text sits prominently below it on the purple floor.

A dark Pizza Hut title card appears first, with the familiar red roof shape above large white “Pizza Hut” lettering. As the logo fades, it reveals an animated fantasy ballroom scene from Disney’s “Beauty and the Beast.” A golden chandelier glows overhead, pink streamers arch down from above, and rows of enchanted dishes and household objects line both sides like performers. In the center, animated castle servants dance: Cogsworth, the brown clock character with a round face and little clock hands, steps forward grinning; Mrs. Potts, the lavender-and-white teapot, and Chip, the small teacup, appear nearby; then Lumiere, the golden candlestick with candle-flame hands, takes center stage under the chandelier. The scene is bright, busy, and magical, with bubbles floating through the dark blue background and warm golden light sparkling around the characters. The animation changes to a top-down view of Mrs. Potts on a polished reddish-brown floor, surrounded in a circle by six small golden candle-like figures with blue bands and glowing flames. She turns and smiles as the little flames form a ring around her. A small white copyright notice for Walt Disney appears in the lower right. The commercial then shows another animated castle interior: a tall pink wardrobe-like character with a smiling face stands at the left, while other enchanted household characters move around in a dim, grand hall with staircases, furniture, and warm shadows. A broom or feather-duster-like figure bobs up and down, and small teacup and footstool-like characters gather near the floor. A close-up of the Beast follows. He is an animated, broad-faced, lion-like creature with brown fur, curved horns, thick eyebrows, fangs, and a white shirt under a dark cloak or jacket. He raises a large clawed hand toward the viewer, first with a mischievous grin and then with his mouth open wide, showing his teeth. The Beast image dissolves into a real child’s play scene. A blond boy, about early elementary-school age, smiles warmly in a softly lit home setting. He holds up a Beast puppet beside his face. The puppet is a small figure of the Beast in a dark purple coat, white shirt front, and red lower garment; its furry head and raised hands resemble the animated character. The boy looks at it with delight, tilting his head slightly as if making the puppet perform. The scene then shifts to a blond girl of similar age holding a Belle puppet. She wears a red top with a patterned vest or jumper over it. Belle’s puppet has brown hair and a bright yellow ball gown with a wide skirt. The girl gazes at the puppet fondly, smiling as she moves Belle closer to her face, as if admiring or playing with her. A tabletop display presents two of the promotional puppets in the foreground: Cogsworth, the brown clock character with a golden face and hands raised, stands on the left, and Chip, the smiling teacup with a small chip in the rim, stands on the right. Large white text in the upper right reads “$1.49.” Along the bottom, small white text says, “One available each week while supplies last at participating restaurants.” Behind the tabletop, tall windowpanes show a dark blue night outside. In the background, the Belle and Beast puppets move into view and settle beside the others, so all four characters—Beast, Belle, Cogsworth, and Chip—are visible together, with Chip closest to the front right. A “Beauty and the Beast” videocassette case appears upright on the tabletop. The cover art shows Belle in her yellow gown looking up at the Beast in a blue coat, with other enchanted characters below them. The title “Walt Disney Classic Beauty and the Beast” is printed prominently in gold and white on a purple-blue background. A hand enters from the right and pulls out a rectangular card from behind the cassette. The card has a red border, a Pizza Hut logo, and large black text reading “VALUE CARD,” with several smaller bullet-point offers printed beneath. The hand holds the card in front of the cassette so the Pizza Hut branding and “VALUE CARD” heading are clear. A wider product display then shows the videocassette standing behind the value card on the tabletop. White text along the bottom reads, “Full details inside cassette. Video cassette not available at Pizza Hut restaurants.” The children appear together in the home setting, smiling and playing with the puppets. The boy holds the Beast puppet in front of him while the girl holds Belle. They bring the two figures close together as if acting out a scene. Both children look happy and absorbed, grinning as the puppets sway and face each other. The girl’s Belle puppet, with its shiny yellow skirt, moves in front of the boy’s Beast puppet, and the two children continue to animate them by hand. The final images return to the romantic “Beauty and the Beast” world. The Beast and Belle figures appear side by side against a dark, theatrical background, then the scene becomes an animated ballroom. Belle, in her full golden gown, and the Beast, now in a royal blue coat, stand arm in arm beneath a huge glowing chandelier. They face away from the viewer and move together into an enormous golden hall lined with tall columns, arched windows, and draped balconies. The chandelier hangs low and luminous at the center, while the ceiling and walls shimmer with warm amber light, ending the commercial on the grand ballroom fantasy.

A young blonde girl with tight curly hair sits in a bright, busy McDonald’s dining area. She smiles straight ahead, holding both hands up near her face as if showing them off. A drink cup with a straw sits in front of her on the table. Over the lower part of the scene, the word “Nostalgia” appears in white, alongside the McDonald’s golden arches logo. Another child, a young boy with light brown hair, moves into view beside her. excerpt: A studio scene opens on a male-presenting adult performer with a white-painted, mask-like face and a calm, serious expression. He stands against a plain blue-gray background, dressed like a stylized juggler or clown: a tall yellow cone hat, a pale gray long coat, a large yellow bow tie, yellow trousers, and oversized patch pockets decorated in gray and yellow patterns. One pocket has a grid design, another has diagonal stripes, and another has large yellow dots. He juggles several small rectangular transistor radios, tossing them in smooth arcs above his hands and even above his hat. The radios are different colors, including white, yellow, brown, and dark-toned models, with circular dials and small speaker faces visible as they turn. The image moves in tight to one of his coat pockets, the gray-and-yellow grid pocket. A small white radio drops neatly into it, leaving only the top edge and part of a black circular dial peeking out. The pocket bulges slightly around the radio. After a pause, the view shifts across the front of his coat to another patch pocket, this one gray with bold yellow diagonal stripes. Another small radio slides into this pocket, again sticking out just enough to show its top and dial area. Attention then goes to the dotted pocket on the performer’s chest, gray with large yellow circles. A white RCA Victor portable radio rises into view from inside this pocket, its round tuning dial prominent near the top. Large white on-screen lettering reading “RCA VICTOR” appears across the lower part of the image. A hand reaches in, grips the radio by the dial area, and pulls it out. As it emerges, the radio’s front is shown clearly: a rectangular white case, a large ribbed speaker grille across the lower half, a circular tuning dial near the top, and small controls on the side. The hand sets the radio upright on a smooth white rounded surface, propping it with a small fold-out stand so it leans back slightly. The hand rests on the circular dial as if demonstrating or adjusting it. The demonstration changes to batteries. Two hands appear against the same plain studio background, tossing small red-and-black cylindrical batteries. A soft yellow cone hat, matching the performer’s hat, is held open like a basket. Batteries drop into the hat one after another. After several have gone in, a hand reaches down inside the hat and rummages around. It pulls out a small handful of three red RCA-branded batteries, their round RCA logos visible on the labels, and holds them together in the palm. The RCA Victor radio is then shown held horizontally in both hands, with its front facing outward. The white case has the circular tuning dial on the right side, a round speaker grille in the middle, a small red button or indicator to the left, and an open battery compartment on the side. The demonstrator brings the red RCA batteries to the open compartment and loads them in. As this happens, large bold white text appears over the radio reading “4 times longer,” with a pale blue-green shadow that makes the words stand out. The hands continue placing or adjusting the batteries at the side of the radio while the “4 times longer” text remains over the product. The performer reappears, again juggling the portable radios in front of the plain blue-gray background. His face remains composed and focused as the radios rotate through the air over his hands and hat. The scene then shifts to a low view of a flat studio surface. Several non-RCA radios or radio parts hit the floor and break apart. Yellow and white casing pieces, wires, and internal components scatter. A dark radio falls and bursts open, exposing its inside parts. In contrast, a white RCA Victor radio drops onto the same surface. It bounces and flips, but remains in one piece. It rotates through the air, lands on a corner, and settles intact, leaning diagonally with its speaker grille and circular dial still visible. Large white lettering appears around it: “non-breakable” at the top and “IMPAC case” at the bottom, presenting the case as durable. The juggler returns once more, still in his pale gray coat with yellow accents, tossing the small radios in a steady pattern. He catches and releases them with open hands, the radios flashing their dials and colored cases as they turn. The product lineup appears on a blue-gray surface. First, one pale mint or light green RCA Victor portable radio rests at the upper left, lying at a slight angle with its circular tuning dial on top and speaker grille visible. A copper-brown version slides or appears at the lower right, similarly shaped with a round dial and front grille. A white version then joins at the lower left. The three radios form a loose triangular arrangement, showing the model in three different colors. The commercial ends on the RCA Victor brand mark against a blue background. Large white text reads “RCA VICTOR.” Beneath it are the round red RCA logo and the familiar “His Master’s Voice” image: a white dog sitting and listening to a horn gramophone. The words “HIS MASTER’S VOICE” appear in quotation marks below the image.

A young blonde woman in a red-and-white checked dress appears in a warmly lit boy’s bedroom. She has a neat 1950s bob with short bangs, small earrings, and dark-framed eyeglasses resting on top of her head like a headband. She turns from the side toward the viewer, speaking directly as if making her case. Behind her are teenage-style room decorations: a triangular pennant on the wall with the letters “LFC,” framed pictures, a sailing-ship print, snapshots, and a telescope near the bed. She gestures to herself with one hand, then brings a hand to her chest, looking confident and slightly playful. As the view widens, a young fair-haired boy is visible tucked into bed beside her. He lies propped on white pillows, wearing patterned pajamas, with a blanket pulled up. The woman sits near the foot or side of the bed, holding a small dark bottle or container with a light cap, visually connected with the “pill” mentioned in the audio context. She turns from addressing the viewer to the child, reaches over, and gently strokes his forehead. The boy looks tired and passive, rubbing at his face and resting against the pillows. The woman then turns back outward, still holding the small container, raising her free hand in a poised, explanatory gesture. A second woman is introduced in a different child’s bedroom. She is also blonde, with fuller curled hair, and wears a dark green turtleneck sweater. She smiles warmly and looks down toward a child off to one side, then turns toward the viewer with a calm, assured expression. The room around her is softer and more traditionally feminine: pale walls, a white ornate headboard, sheer ruffled fabric near the bed, framed nursery-style pictures, a bedside lamp, a panda toy, and dolls arranged in the background. The second woman steps beside a little girl lying in bed under white covers. The girl has brown hair cut in a bob with bangs and wears a light-colored, ruffled nightgown. The woman brings a baby doll toward her, while also holding a small dark jar with a pale lid. She leans over the bed smiling, offering the doll and the jar into the child’s space. The girl looks up at her and takes interest in the doll. The woman continues smiling at close range, creating a gentle bedside-care moment. She holds the jar where the girl can see it, then lets the girl hold or touch it while the doll rests near the child. The scene returns to the first blonde woman in the checked dress. She is now closer to the viewer, with the boy’s bed and lamp behind her. She speaks directly, her expression alert and persuasive, while the boy lies in the background. At one point the boy is partly hidden by a white bedcover or pillow as he shifts. The woman looks from him back to the viewer, then turns toward him with a pleased smile. A close view shows the little girl from the second room holding the dark jar near her face, with her doll beside her; she smiles faintly as an adult hand steadies or adjusts the jar. This briefly emphasizes the Vicks jar as something the child recognizes and accepts. The checked-dress woman continues addressing the viewer with the boy resting behind her. She looks earnest, then raises her hand in a precise “OK” gesture, holding up a tiny white tablet between her fingers. The pill is very small against her hand, and she presents it close to her face as if demonstrating how simple or modern it is. Her eyes are wide and focused on the viewer, and the eyeglasses remain perched on her head. The second woman in the green turtleneck then appears seated beside the little girl again. She smiles and speaks while resting one hand near the child’s collar. She holds the Vicks jar upright, its dark body and light lid clearly visible, then positions it in front of her chest as she explains. The child reclines on the pillow, looking up at her, while a baby doll lies across the blanket nearby. The woman unscrews or opens the jar, dips a finger in, and brings a small amount of ointment toward the child. Her movements are slow and careful, focused on comfort rather than urgency. She gently opens the neckline of the girl’s ruffled nightgown and begins rubbing the ointment onto the child’s upper chest. The child remains still, looking downward and then relaxing. In a close view, the woman’s hand moves in smooth strokes over the girl’s chest, just below the collarbone, while the doll’s face is visible beside them. The girl’s expression softens; her eyes drift partly closed and her mouth settles into a small, contented smile. The adult hand continues the rubbing motion across the chest, then eases away as the child tilts her chin slightly upward, appearing soothed. The view widens again to the bedside scene. The woman in green finishes adjusting the girl’s nightgown and blanket, still smiling. The girl sits more upright in bed, and the woman’s hands rest reassuringly on her shoulders and chest area. The woman then looks outward toward the viewer with a composed, maternal expression while keeping one hand protectively on the child. The girl leans closer to her, and the woman gathers her into a hug. The little girl sits up within the white covers, nestled against the woman’s chest. The woman kisses the child on the forehead or temple, then both smile. The child cuddles in, clutching close to the woman, and the woman beams directly outward before looking down affectionately at the girl. A bedside lamp fills the scene next. It has a pale lampshade and a shiny, dark metal base. A hand reaches under the shade near the switch, fingers sliding around the lamp stem as if turning it off or adjusting it for bedtime, then withdraws. The lamp remains the central object for a moment, reinforcing the nighttime setting. The final view settles on the Vicks VapoRub jar placed on a polished bedside table in front of the lamp base. The jar is dark blue or black with a pale greenish lid and a cream-colored label. The label reads “Vicks VapoRub,” with smaller text below including “Vaporizing Ointment” and “Relieves distress of colds.” At the very end, large white words appear to the right of the jar: “most comforting thing you can do for a cold.” The product remains prominently displayed beside the warm bedside lamp, visually linking it with nighttime care and comfort.

A brightly colored studio set appears against a plain green background. Across the lower part of the set are fluffy white cloud-like shapes and flat, oversized Chevrolet bowtie silhouettes in pale beige and green. In the center, a red sign with large white letters reads “CHEVROLET.” A small “Not For Broadcast” label is visible near the upper left, and a timecode box sits near the lower left. Two adult presenters enter and stand on the central bowtie-shaped platform. The man has dark, neatly combed hair and wears a deep red blazer, white shirt, light green tie, tan trousers, and dark shoes. The woman has short, curled blonde hair and wears a bright magenta blouse with a small brooch, a wide dark full skirt that flares outward, and matching high heels. She holds or brushes the skirt as it swishes, revealing flashes of pink lining. They smile and face forward as if addressing the audience, standing side by side on the raised shape amid the cloud-like scenery. The view alternates between them. The man is shown closer, looking forward and speaking with a composed, cheerful expression; the woman stands just to his side at first, smiling toward him. Then the focus shifts to the woman alone. She sits or perches slightly, hands near her lap, smiling directly forward in the same green studio space, her dark skirt spread around her. The two are then seen full-length again on the platform. They step apart in opposite directions along the set’s flat geometric shapes, moving like dancers. The man walks left and the woman walks right, both keeping their balance on the raised pieces. They turn back toward each other, the woman’s skirt swinging in a wide circle as she pivots. From farther back, the whole stage composition is visible: green backdrop, white clouds, bowtie shapes, and the red “CHEVROLET” sign below them. Large white characters reading “’59” appear high above the presenters. Both of them raise an arm upward toward the number, drawing attention to it. Almost immediately, the image cuts to a shiny 1959 Chevrolet in a simple studio setting: a pale green car seen from the rear three-quarter angle, with long horizontal lines, prominent tailfins, oval rear lights, chrome trim, whitewall tires, and a glossy floor beneath it. The car is stationary and displayed like a featured product. The view returns to the presenters on the Chevrolet set with “’59” still above them, their arms lifted toward the text. The woman is then shown closer again, seated and smiling broadly, with the white cloud shapes behind her. The man appears in a similar close view, seated with one knee raised and one arm resting casually, smiling toward the audience. They continue appearing separately in close views, both maintaining friendly expressions and polished stage posture. The man rises or leans forward slightly, speaking directly forward. He gestures subtly with one hand as he stands against the green background, his red blazer and green tie matching the set’s color scheme. The woman follows in close view, smiling and facing forward, her dark full skirt filling the lower part of the image. Both presenters stand again on the red central pedestal above the large “CHEVROLET” sign. The man steps up first, and the woman moves beside him, placing a hand lightly near his shoulder as they stand close together. They face forward, then glance toward one another. The woman’s skirt continues to ripple as she shifts her feet. They smile together on the pedestal, framed by the green backdrop and cloud shapes. They then sit on either side of the central platform above the “CHEVROLET” sign, the man on the left and the woman on the right. Another car appears briefly: a pink or rose-colored Chevrolet station wagon or sedan-wagon viewed from the rear three-quarter angle. It has chrome bumpers, tailfins, whitewall tires, and a rear license plate that reads “C1959.” The car sits still in a studio display area with a light floor and neutral background. The scene returns to the two presenters seated on the Chevrolet set. The presenters move again across the bowtie shapes. The man steps along the platform while the woman turns, her skirt lifting outward in a circular flare. They then lean over a beige part of the set, both smiling toward the audience, their upper bodies resting casually on the flat shape as if it were a counter or railing. The woman gestures downward and forward, then both begin to rise. Standing side by side, the man extends one hand outward in a presenting gesture while the woman faces forward, smiling. They come together closely, his arm around or behind her, and both look out toward the audience. Large white text appears above them: “THURS. OCT. 16.” The woman lifts a hand near her face in a small wave or flourish beneath the date. They look at each other briefly, then face forward again, smiling. The date text disappears, leaving the green backdrop. The two remain close together, the woman’s full dark skirt spreading out in a bell shape. The man gestures with one hand while standing slightly angled toward her, then both stand centered on the red pedestal. As the view widens, the large white “’59” reappears above them, and the red “CHEVROLET” sign is visible below. They stand upright and still for a moment, framed symmetrically by the clouds and bowtie shapes. The pair glance at one another under the “’59,” then face front again. The woman extends one arm outward to the side in a graceful presenting pose. Another brief product display follows: a pale green and white 1959 Chevrolet seen from the rear side, again emphasizing the long body, tailfins, chrome trim, and whitewall tires on a glossy studio floor. The commercial returns to the presenters on the Chevrolet set, arms opened slightly as if presenting the car and the brand, with “’59” overhead and the large “CHEVROLET” sign below.

The commercial begins in black and white with a sunny Florida orange grove. Rows of citrus trees frame a path, with leafy branches heavy with round oranges on both sides. The sun glows high above the trees. Large white serif letters spelling “Florida” appear across the grove, then the image changes to orange branches surrounding a tall glass of orange juice. The glass is centered among the fruit and leaves, with the word “Florida” faintly printed on it. Bold white lettering grows over the glass: “POWERHOUSE OF VITAMIN C,” filling much of the screen before fading away. The glass and branches fade into an outdoor ice rink. A young woman figure skater, identified by on-screen text as “BARBARA ANN SCOTT,” skates across the ice in a dark skating dress with a short skirt and white skates. Bare winter trees, benches, and tall lamp posts stand in the background, suggesting a public park rink. She glides forward, jumps with arms raised, and lands on the ice. The view becomes focused on her lower legs and skates as she performs quick footwork, the blades cutting across the smooth surface and kicking up a misty spray of ice. The skating scene fades into a tidy domestic kitchen. A blonde woman with curled, shoulder-length 1950s-style hair stands beside a wall oven set into a brick or tile wall. She wears a fitted long-sleeved sweater with a small collar or neckline detail and a pearl-like necklace. In the foreground on a counter is a serving tray holding a large can labeled “Orange Juice” and several filled glasses. She turns from the oven toward the counter, smiles, and faces forward as if addressing the viewer. Behind her are cabinets and shelves with dishes, reinforcing the home kitchen setting. She moves closer to the tray, rests a hand near it, and then selects one glass of orange juice. The glass is tall and filled nearly to the top with a light-colored, opaque juice. She lifts it to eye level, looks at it appreciatively, and continues speaking while holding it beside her face. Her expression is pleasant and confident. She smiles warmly, then glances down at the glass again, presenting it as something attractive and refreshing. The image then changes to a store-like display of many large cans arranged in rows. Each can has bold lettering reading “Orange Juice,” with “FLORIDA” printed beneath. The labels also show small pictures of an orange and a glass of juice. At the bottom of the labels, small text appears to read “Your choice of brands.” A wire shopping basket or cart edge is visible in front. A hand reaches in from above and lifts one large can from the row, while another hand steadies it from below. The can is brought forward, filling the foreground so the label “Orange Juice” and “FLORIDA” are clear. The display fades back to a polished serving tray on a countertop. A large can of Florida orange juice stands in the middle, surrounded by multiple full glasses of juice arranged around it, visually suggesting that one can serves many glasses. The tray has a shiny rim and small feet, and the filled glasses catch the light along their tops. Large white text overlays the tray and product: “POWERHOUSE OF NATURAL VITAMIN C.” The words dominate the center of the image, with the can and glasses still visible behind them. As the commercial ends, the text fades, leaving a closer view of the can and the full glasses. Finally, the word “Florida” appears again in large white serif letters over the glasses, with a bright sparkle near the top of one glass, closing on the product’s Florida identity.

The commercial is in black and white. It opens on a polished tabletop arranged like an elegant still life. Around the Yuban can are wine bottles, a decanter, several wine glasses, tall pepper-mill-like grinders, and covered dishes. The coffee beans form a dark, pebbled carpet across the foreground. The cup remains near the can, while the wine glasses and bottles fill the left side of the arrangement. As the display continues, more foods appear: a cheese board with a round cheese and cut pieces, a dish of grapes or small fruit, and a basket holding bottles and glasses. The setting looks staged and abundant, with brick or tiled wall texture in the background and reflective tabletop surfaces. The food display expands further to include a large steak or roast on a grill-like tray in the foreground. It is placed beside the cheeses and wine, with a lidded serving vessel behind it. The steak’s surface is highlighted, and the surrounding props—bottles, glasses, cheese, and fruit—suggest rich, mature, carefully chosen foods. The Yuban can is no longer central in this part; the food and drink examples dominate the table. The image changes to a close-up of coffee beans filling the entire screen. The beans are oval, ridged, and densely piled, with light catching their curved surfaces. The texture of the beans becomes the main visual focus. Then the product arrangement returns: the Yuban can and the filled cup sit again among loose beans. A hand enters from the right, grasping the handle of the white cup. The hand lifts the cup from its saucer, leaving the saucer behind on the bean-covered cloth. The cup rises past the wine glasses and decanter in the background. A light-skinned adult woman appears in profile as the cup is brought to her lips. She has neatly styled 1950s hair, swept back with curled detail near the ear, and wears decorative earrings. Her face is calm and composed. Holding the cup delicately by the handle, she leans in and sips. Her eyes are lowered toward the cup. After drinking, she remains poised, with a faint satisfied expression as the cup hovers near her mouth. The scene returns to the product still life: the Yuban can with its oval “YUBAN COFFEE” label sits beside the white cup on its saucer, both surrounded by coffee beans and soft cloth. The background again includes the elegant table objects, such as a covered dish and tall mills. A new demonstration begins with an open burlap sack filled with coffee beans. Hands scoop up beans from the sack and let them fall back in a small stream. Large white on-screen text appears over the sack reading “green beans.” The hands continue stirring and lifting the beans, emphasizing their small, pale, raw-looking appearance in the black-and-white image. The coarse weave of the burlap sack frames the mound. The comparison widens into two side-by-side bean displays. On the left, a hand holds a scoop or cloth full of darker beans, labeled with large white text “aged beans.” On the right, another hand holds a lighter-looking handful labeled “green beans.” The two labels sit near the bottom of the screen, each aligned with its respective sample. The left-hand aged beans appear darker and richer in tone, while the right-hand green beans appear lighter. Behind them, sacks of coffee beans are stacked, and a worker, seen from behind in a plaid shirt, moves among the sacks in a warehouse-like storage space. The hands hold the two samples forward for comparison while the worker and sacks remain in the background. The focus tightens to a close-up of hands cupping a mound of the darker aged beans. The beans fill the palms, piled high, with individual ridges and rounded shapes clearly visible. The hands tilt slightly, and the beans begin to cascade forward. The falling beans visually transform into a filled white coffee cup: the stream of beans gives way to the dark surface of coffee inside the cup. Small pale bubbles or highlights float on the coffee’s surface. A hand steadies the cup and saucer near the rim and edge, presenting the drink close to the viewer. The cup remains in close-up, full of dark coffee with a few light bubbles on top. Fingers hover and adjust around the cup and saucer, then the cup is lifted. The background becomes darker and softer, and the cup moves toward a person in formal clothing. A light-skinned adult man appears, clean-shaven, with neatly combed dark hair. He wears a dark suit jacket, a light dress shirt, and a tie. He holds the white cup by its handle at chest level, looking down toward it. His expression is restrained and thoughtful. He raises the cup to his lips and sips, keeping his posture upright. The background behind him is softly lit and patterned with bright highlights, suggesting an elegant interior. The image returns one final time to the product arrangement. The Yuban Coffee can is placed on the left, its “YUBAN COFFEE” label clearly visible, and the white cup of coffee sits on a saucer to the right. Both rest on the spread of coffee beans and textured cloth. In the background are the same refined table props: glassware, a covered dish, and tall mills. The composition holds steady on the can and cup, with the beans filling the foreground and the product name prominently displayed.

In black and white, a well-dressed adult man appears briefly in a studio-like setting, wearing a dark suit, light shirt, and tie. He stands in front of a background with repeated “Van Heusen” signs, with a few people faintly visible behind him. The scene quickly gives way to bold graphic animation: bright, angular white shapes move across a plain gray background like folded pieces of cloth or a stylized collar. Across the lower part of the image, large lettering reads, “won’t wrinkle...ever!” A small comic figure appears beside the collar, perched on the mannequin’s right shoulder area. The scene changes to a domestic ironing area. Only the torso and arms of a woman are visible. She wears a dress with a fitted waist and a light decorative band or apron-like detail around the middle; a laundry basket sits in the background. A white shirt is spread across an ironing board in the foreground. She lifts and arranges the shirt fabric with both hands, smoothing it out across the board. A young adult man appears in an interior room, wearing a white dress shirt and a tie. He has neatly combed short hair and stands against a wall with a framed picture on the left. He holds a black telephone receiver to his ear, the coiled cord hanging down. His shirt looks smooth and fresh, with the collar sitting neatly around his neck. Large bold lettering appears over the display inside a rectangular outline: “Van Heusen Century Shirts.” The text dominates the upper half of the image while the mannequin shirt remains centered beneath it. The small figure remains partly visible beside the letters and the collar. The final product display holds on the white shirt and tie beneath the large “Van Heusen Century Shirts” name. The collar remains smooth and symmetrical around the black neck form. A rectangular Kodak package appears first, floating against a soft gray studio background. The box is light-toned with the word “Kodak” printed large on the long side and again on the top, with a dark checkerboard-like band along the bottom edge. As the package fades away, it gives way to a staged home exterior or patio setting. Ozzie, a clean-shaven adult man with neatly combed dark hair, stands in front of a house façade with multi-pane windows, low shrubs, and leafy plants. He wears a tailored suit jacket, a light shirt, a dark tie, and a pocket square. He holds a compact, box-shaped Kodak Brownie Turret movie camera in both hands at chest height. The camera has a shiny rectangular body, a small viewfinder on top, and a distinctive cluster of three round lenses mounted together on the front. He looks down at the camera while walking slightly across the set, then turns toward the viewer and presents it with a friendly, demonstrative expression. He brings the camera closer to his body and begins showing its controls. His hands rotate and point around the front lens assembly. The view moves in close to the camera itself: the metal body fills most of the image, with Ozzie’s suit fabric behind it. His fingers steady the side while his other hand points to the circular lenses. The three lenses are arranged like a small triangular cluster on a rotating turret, with one lens positioned for use and the others nearby. He indicates one lens, then another, making clear that each circular opening has a different purpose. He turns the turret with his fingertips, and the lens cluster rotates so a different lens comes into position at the front of the camera. After demonstrating the lenses, Ozzie lifts the camera to his eye. The scene changes to what the camera is aimed at: a backyard game in progress. Two young male players, likely teenagers or young adults, stand on opposite sides of a badminton net. One is farther away on the left, wearing a light shirt and light trousers; the other is nearer on the right, seen mostly from behind in a short-sleeved shirt and trousers. A white picket fence runs behind the net, with shrubs and trees beyond it. The players hold rackets and rally a small shuttlecock back and forth. In this first view, the whole playing area is visible, including both players, the net, and much of the fence and yard. The image returns to Ozzie in front of the windows and bushes. He lowers the camera, smiles, and continues explaining. He turns the turret again, keeping the camera in both hands at mid-chest. Then he raises it once more to his eye, bracing it with one hand underneath and the other at the side. The backyard game appears again, now framed more tightly on the player across the net. He stands with his legs apart behind the net, holding his racket ready, and the picket fence and foliage fill the background. He moves the racket across his body as the shuttlecock comes toward him, then shifts his stance to continue the play. In a rectangular box near the lower center, white text reads “THE ORIGINAL” above a large script “Shower Massage,” with “BY TELEDYNE” underneath.
